definition_zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的
definition_en: suitable and correct for a situation, belonging to one thing alone, or, in grammar, naming a particular person or place
core_image: 一件东西落进专为它留出的那个位置，不偏不倚，正正好好
scene: 正式晚宴前，主人把刀叉一件件摆正，餐巾折好放在盘子左侧。She checked that every guest had the proper glass beside the plate.
sceneCN: 这里取「适当的、合乎场合的」意思（第 1 个义项：适合当时场合与规矩的）；句意为她逐一确认每位客人的盘边都放着该配的那只酒杯。摆正刀叉的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的

derivatives.zh: 由 proper 加 -ly 构成，义为「适当地；正确地」
由拉丁 proprietas 经法语进入英语，义为「财产；性质」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprietas，义为「得体；礼节」
在拉丁词干 propri- 前加 ad-，义为「合适的」

senses.title: Suitable and correct for the situation
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular situation, purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种场合、用途或某人来说正确或合适的
senses.example: Use the proper tool for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 干这活要用合适的工具。
senses.why: Latin proprius meant one's own, and what belongs to a thing is exactly what fits it, so the sense slid from belonging to being the right one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，而属于某物的东西恰恰就是适合它的东西，于是词义从「属于」滑到「正是该用的那一个」。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing alone
senses.definition: belonging by nature to one particular thing, person or group and not to any other
senses.definitionCN: 天然属于某一特定事物、人或群体，而不属于其他
senses.example: This bird is proper to the island and lives nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟是该岛特有的，别处见不到。
senses.why: The root sense of own is plainest here: a quality proper to something is a quality that belongs to it and to nothing else, which is why the word so often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: 「自己的」这层本义在这里最清楚：proper to 某物的性质，就是只属于它、不属于别处的性质，所以这个词常与 to 连用。

senses.title: Strictly so called
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean the central part of a place or thing, as opposed to the area around it
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指某地或某物的中心部分，以区别于其外围
senses.example: The market lies outside the old town proper.
senses.exampleCN: 市场位于老城区本身之外。
senses.why: If something is its own, the word can mark the thing itself as against its outskirts, and that is exactly how the after-noun use arose.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物是「它自己的」，这个词就能标出「事物本身」以区别于外围；后置用法正是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Naming one particular individual
senses.definition: in grammar, naming a particular person, place or thing rather than a whole class of them
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指称某个特定的人、地或物，而不是一整类
senses.example: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
senses.exampleCN: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。
senses.why: A proper noun belongs to a single bearer instead of a whole class, so the grammatical term preserves the old idea of exclusive ownership.
senses.whyCN: 专有名词只属于一个承担者而不属于一整类，所以这个语法术语保留的仍是「排他地拥有」这层旧义。

senses.title: Socially correct and respectable
senses.definition: behaving in the way polite society considers correct and respectable
senses.definitionCN: 按照讲究礼数的社会所认可、体面的方式行事
senses.example: It is not proper to ask about someone's salary.
senses.exampleCN: 打听别人的薪水不合规矩。
senses.why: A community decides what belongs to a well-run occasion, so propriety became a matter of manners and the adjective took on the sense of socially correct.
senses.whyCN: 一个共同体认定什么才属于「办得体面的场合」，于是 proper 也成了举止问题，形容词便带上「合乎社交规矩」的意思。

intro.en: Proper goes back to a Latin adjective meaning one's own, and every later sense is a variation on belonging.
intro.cn: proper 上溯到一个意为「自己的」的拉丁形容词，后来所有义项都是「归属」这一点的变奏。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, personal, not shared with others; a common but uncertain explanation derives it from pro privo, for a private person.
items.cn: proprius 意为自己的、个人的、不与他人共有的；一般认为它与 pro privo（为了私人）有关，但这一解释并不确定。

items.en: The noun proprietas named ownership and also the quality that belongs to a thing and makes it what it is.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 指所有权，也指属于某物、使该物成为其自身的性质。

items.en: Old French propre kept the senses of one's own, suitable and also clean or neat.
items.cn: 古法语 propre 保留了「自己的」「合适的」，以及「干净整洁的」这几层意思。

items.en: Middle English proper first meant belonging to someone or something, and older texts also use it for fine or excellent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 proper 最初指「属于某人或某物的」，较早的文本里还用它表示「出色的、优良的」。

items.en: Modern English settles on suitable, exclusive and strict, and keeps the old ownership in property, propriety, appropriate and the grammatical proper noun.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义定为「合适的、专属的、严格意义上的」，并把「归属」的旧义留在 property、propriety、appropriate 以及语法术语 proper noun 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for one's own; the near-meaning group gathers words about fitting and good manners.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「自己的」形容词上的词；近义组收关于「合适」与「礼节」的词。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from ownership and ends in fitness, and the whole family still turns on the question of what belongs where.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「归属」出发，走到「合宜」，整族词始终围绕「什么该在什么位置」这一问题。

normal.en: Latin proprius means one's own, so proper is about ownership before it is ever about manners.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，所以 proper 先说归属，之后才说礼节。

normal.en: Property and propriety share the same stem: what one owns, and what it is fitting to own or to do.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同一词干：一个是拥有的东西，一个是拥有或行事是否得体。

normal.en: The grammatical proper noun keeps the old sense, since such a name is owned by one person or one place.
normal.cn: 语法术语 proper noun 保留了旧义，因为这类名字只被一个人或一个地方拥有。

normal.en: After a noun, as in the city proper, the word marks the thing itself rather than the area around it.
normal.cn: 放在名词后，如 the city proper，这个词标出的是事物本身，而不是它周边的地带。

normal.en: Appropriate adds ad-, to, to the same stem: to make something one's own, and therefore to make it fit.
normal.cn: appropriate 在同一词干前加 ad-（向），意为「使成为自己的」，因此也就是「使之合宜」。

abstract.en: What is proper to a thing is what cannot be taken from it without changing what it is.
abstract.cn: 某物所专属的东西，一旦被拿走，它就不再是原来的它。

abstract.en: Manners and grammar seem far apart, yet both use proper to decide what belongs where.
abstract.cn: 礼节与语法看似相隔很远，却都用 proper 来判定什么该在什么位置。

abstract.en: A word for ownership became a word for correctness because fitting in has always been a matter of belonging.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有」的词变成了表示「正确」的词，因为「合宜」从来就是「归属」的另一面。

examples.en: Use the proper tool for the job.
examples.cn: 干这活要用合适的工具。

examples.en: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
examples.cn: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging, and the senses fan out from it: what fits because it belongs, what belongs to one thing only, the thing itself, a name owned by one bearer, and the manners a community expects.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「归属」，义项由它散开：因为属于所以合宜、只属于一物的特性、事物本身、只被一个对象拥有的名字，以及共同体期待的礼节。

core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西落进专为它挖出的那个凹槽，四边不留缝隙。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of ownership and the noun built from it hold the word together, and English suffixes turn the same stem into adverbs, nouns and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 表示归属的拉丁语形容词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，英语后缀又把同一词干变成副词、名词和相关形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius, one's own, and the noun proprietas, ownership or peculiar quality, are the direct sources of the English word and of its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 proprius（自己的）与名词 proprietas（所有权、特性）是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地
definition_en: in the correct or suitable way; in a socially acceptable manner; (British, informal) completely or thoroughly
core_image: 工匠把一块木板量准、放平，直到它与墙面严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子贴紧墙边，反复对照图纸，确认每一块板都装在该在的位置。The carpenter checked the shelf twice to make sure it was properly fixed to the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 properly 是「正确地、恰当地」（第 1 个义项：以正确合适的方式）；句意为木匠检查了两次，确认搁板被牢牢固定在墙上。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、图纸、木搁板。

pos.zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到形容词，义为「恰当的；正确的；本身的」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprius（自己的），义为「得体的举止；合宜」
同出拉丁 proprius（属于自己的东西），义为「财产；房产；属性」
proper 前加否定前缀 im-，义为「不恰当的；不合规矩的」

senses.title: In the correct or suitable way
senses.definition: in the way that is correct, suitable, or expected for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 以正确、合适或符合某一用途所需的方式
senses.example: The machine will not work unless it is properly connected.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器如果没有正确接通，就无法运转。
senses.why: Properly is simply proper plus -ly, so it carries the old Latin sense of something sitting in its own place and fitting there exactly.
senses.whyCN: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，因此继承了拉丁语「待在自己位置、恰好贴合」的意思：装在该装的地方，才算正确地做。

senses.title: In a socially acceptable manner
senses.definition: in a way that follows good manners or accepted social standards
senses.definitionCN: 遵循良好礼节或公认社会标准的方式
senses.example: He was properly introduced to the guests before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚宴前，他被正式介绍给各位客人。
senses.why: If a thing belongs in its proper place, a person can also belong in the proper occasion, so the word slides from a fitted joint to fitted behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 东西有它该在的位置，人也有他该在场的场合，于是词义便从「装得对」滑向「举止合宜」。

senses.title: Completely; thoroughly (British, informal)
senses.titleCN: 彻底地；完全地（英式口语）
senses.definition: used in British informal speech to mean completely or very much
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中表示「完全地、非常」
senses.example: I was properly soaked by the time I got home.
senses.exampleCN: 等我到家时，已经浑身湿透了。
senses.why: When a job is done properly, nothing is left half-finished, so speakers began using the word for utterly or entirely, especially in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得 properly，就意味着没有一处半途而废；英式口语便借这层「做得彻底」引申出「完全地」。

senses.title: With good reason; justifiably
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, reasonable, or deserved
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、合理或应得的方式
senses.example: She was properly proud of the garden she had raised from seed.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是她从种子一手养大的，她理应为之自豪。
senses.why: Something proper is fitting, and what is fitting can also be deserved, which lets the word mark fair pride or fair blame rather than mere correctness.
senses.whyCN: proper 指「合宜」，而合宜的东西也就是应得的；于是这个词能标示理所应当的自豪或责备，而不只是「正确」。

intro.en: Properly is the adverb of proper, a word that reached English from Latin proprius by way of French, with -ly added to mark the manner of doing something.
intro.cn: properly 是 proper 的副词形式；proper 经法语来自拉丁语 proprius，加上 -ly 表示做事的方式。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, special, or belonging to a particular thing rather than to others.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、专属的」，指某物属于特定对象，而不属于别的对象。

items.en: The noun proprietas named the quality of belonging to someone, and it later split into English propriety and property.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 表示「归属某人的性质」，后来在英语中分化出 propriety 与 property。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as propre, meaning own, suitable, or clean, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词 propre，意为「自己的、合适的、干净的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English proper meant belonging to a person or thing and also fitting or correct, the sense that survives in proper behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语 proper 既指「属于某人或某物的」，也指「合适的、正确的」，后一义保留在 proper behaviour 中。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to proper, giving properly, which marks the manner of doing something in the right way.
items.cn: 英语在 proper 后加副词后缀 -ly 得到 properly，用来标示「以正确方式做某事」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem proprius; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for doing something the right way.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁词干 proprius 上的词；近义组收表示「以正确方式做事」的副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the ordinary English adverb ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及最常见的英语副词后缀 -ly 组成。

normal.en: Properly is proper plus -ly, and -ly is the ordinary English ending for the manner of an action.
normal.cn: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，而 -ly 是英语里最常见的「做事方式」后缀。

normal.en: Something proper sits in its own place, so doing a job properly means putting every part where it belongs.
normal.cn: proper 的东西待在属于自己的位置，所以把事情做得 properly，就是把每个部分放到该放的地方。

normal.en: Improper is proper with the negative prefix im-, so improper behaviour is the exact opposite of proper behaviour.
normal.cn: improper 是 proper 前加否定前缀 im-，所以不得体的行为正是得体行为的反面。

normal.en: Property and propriety share one stem: one is what belongs to you, the other is what belongs to good manners.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同根：前者是归属于你的东西，后者是归属于良好礼节的东西。

normal.en: The phrase properly speaking marks the strict or exact use of a word, which is the correct sense of the adverb.
normal.cn: 短语 properly speaking 标示一个词的严格、准确用法，这正是这个副词「正确」的一面。

abstract.en: A joint that clicks into place is the whole idea of properly: no force left over, no gap left open.
abstract.cn: 一个卡进槽里的榫头就是 properly 的全部意象：用不上多余的力，也留不下一道缝。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a fitted shelf to a fitting remark, because both are judged by one question: does it belong here?
abstract.cn: 这个词可以从装好的搁板滑到一句合适的话，因为两者面对同一个判断：它属于这里吗？

abstract.en: When British speakers say properly soaked, they mean soaked through, which shows how correctness can slide into completeness.
abstract.cn: 英国人说 properly soaked 时意思是湿透，可见「正确」可以滑向「彻底」。

examples.en: The shelter must be properly anchored before the storm arrives.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，这个庇护所必须被妥善固定。

examples.en: She was properly dressed for the interview.
examples.cn: 她为面试穿得很得体。

examples.en: He was properly ashamed of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他对自己说过的话理当感到羞愧。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fitting into the right place; from there the word spreads to social manners, to complete thoroughness, and to what is deserved.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装进正确的位置」；义项由此扩展到社交礼节、彻底的完成，以及理所应得。

scene: 暴雨来得突然，母亲把外套撑开罩住孩子，自己的后背全湿了。She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
sceneCN: 这里表示「保护、使不受伤害」（第 1 个义项：用身体或物件挡住危险）；句意为她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

collocations.phrase: protect a file with a password

derivatives.zh: 由 protect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「保护；防护物」
由 protect 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「保护的；防护的」

senses.title: To keep someone safe from harm
senses.definition: to put a person or thing out of reach of harm or damage, usually by placing your body or an object between them and the threat
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物挡在伤害够不到的地方，通常以身体或物件横在人与威胁之间
senses.example: He raised his arm to protect the child from the flying glass.
senses.exampleCN: 他抬起手臂，替孩子挡住飞来的玻璃。
senses.why: Latin protegere joins pro-, in front, with tegere, to cover, so the first picture is a layer held on the side where the blow lands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 protegere 由 pro-（在前面）与 tegere（盖住）合成，最早的动作就是把一层遮盖挡在挨打的那一侧。

senses.title: To guard against a danger that cannot be touched
senses.definition: to take measures that stop disease, cold, rust or an attack from doing damage, even when the danger has no shape you can see
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施阻止疾病、寒冷、锈蚀或攻击造成损害，即使这种危险看不见形迹
senses.example: A thin film of oil protects the blade against rust.
senses.exampleCN: 薄薄一层油能防止刀身生锈。
senses.why: A cover works because anything reaching the surface is stopped there, so English moves the same verb from visible blows to frost, germs and rust, which also arrive from outside.
senses.whyCN: 遮盖之所以有效，是因为凡是够到表面的东西都被拦在那里；于是英语把这个动词从看得见的打击挪到霜冻、病菌和锈蚀上——它们同样来自外面。

senses.title: To secure a right or a possession by law or contract
senses.definition: to use laws, rules or insurance so that a person's rights, property or income cannot easily be taken away or lost
senses.definitionCN: 借助法律、规则或保险，使某人的权利、财产或收入不易被夺走或损失
senses.example: The new clause protects tenants from sudden eviction.
senses.exampleCN: 新条款保障租客不被突然赶走。
senses.why: Law and insurance do for a person's interests what a coat does for the body: they set an enforceable barrier in front of something valuable.
senses.whyCN: 法律与保险对人利益的用处，就跟外套对身体的用处一样：在贵重的东西前面立起一道能强制执行的屏障。

senses.title: To restrict who may open a file or device
senses.definition: to keep a file, account or device from being opened or changed by anyone who has not been allowed in
senses.definitionCN: 使文件、账户或设备不能被未获许可的人打开或改动
senses.example: She protected the folder with a password before lending the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 把电脑借出去之前，她先用密码保护了那个文件夹。
senses.why: A password is the newest form of the same cover: it stands at the door of the file, and only those who know it may lift the cover.
senses.whyCN: 密码是这层遮盖最新的形态：它守在文件门口，只有知道它的人才被允许把遮盖掀开。

intro.en: Protect comes from a Latin verb that meant to cover something on its front side, and that covering later hardened into a legal and then a digital barrier.
intro.cn: protect 来自一个意为「在正面盖住」的拉丁动词；这层遮盖后来变硬，先成为法律屏障，再成为数字屏障。

items.en: Tegere meant to cover or to clothe, and it supplied the covering half of the word.
items.cn: tegere 意为覆盖、遮盖，是这个词里「盖住」的那一半。

items.en: Pro- put the covering in front, so protegere meant to hold something over a person and keep harm away.
items.cn: pro- 把遮盖物放到前面，于是 protegere 意为把某物罩在人身上，把伤害挡开。

items.en: The participle protectus described someone already sheltered, and English borrowed exactly this form rather than the plain verb.
items.cn: 分词 protectus 描述已经被遮护住的人，英语借的正是这个形式，而不是光秃秃的动词。

items.en: Protectio named the act of covering and defending, and through French it became the English noun protection.
items.cn: protectio 指遮盖与防卫的行为，经法语演变成英语名词 protection。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century and widened it from a physical cover to legal guarantees and finally to passwords.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入这个动词，把「物理遮盖」扩展到法律保障，最后又扩展到密码。

note.en: The first group is built on the Latin verb for covering, with one word that only shares the prefix and the opening letters; the second group gathers verbs for keeping something safe.
note.cn: 第一组建立在表示「遮盖」的拉丁动词上，其中一个词只共用前缀和开头几个字母；第二组收表示「使免受伤害」的动词。

entries.definition: Serving to keep someone or something safe from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 起保护作用的；防护的。

entries.definition: The act of uncovering something hidden, literally the removal of a cover.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏之物；字面义是「把盖子揭掉」。

entries.definition: A natural covering such as skin or a shell; a technical word that keeps the bare sense of covering.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤、外壳等天然覆盖物；专业用语，保留「覆盖」的本义。

entries.definition: A public expression of disagreement; it shares the prefix pro- and the first letters only, the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表达反对；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To ward off an attack, often with force or with argument.
entries.definitionCN: 击退攻击，常靠武力或言辞。

entries.definition: To watch over someone or something in order to prevent danger.
entries.definitionCN: 看守某人某物以防范危险。

entries.definition: To put something solid between a person and a threat.
entries.definitionCN: 把实体挡在人与威胁之间。

entries.definition: To protect something important through careful rules or measures.
entries.definitionCN: 通过周密的规定或措施保护重要之物。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps one picture: a cover held on the side the blow comes from, whether the blow is rain, rust, a lawsuit or a stranger at a keyboard.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词始终保留一幅画面：遮盖挡在打击来的那一侧，不管打击是雨、锈、官司，还是键盘那端的陌生人。

normal.en: Pro- means in front and tegere means to cover, so protect is literally to cover something on its front.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前面」，tegere 意为「盖住」，所以 protect 字面上就是「在正面盖住」。

normal.en: Detect turns the picture around: de- takes the cover away, so to detect is to uncover what was hidden.
normal.cn: detect 把这幅画反过来：de- 把盖子拿走，所以 detect 是揭开被藏着的东西。

normal.en: Protection is the noun of the covering, protector is the person who holds it, and protective is the quality of being able to hold it.
normal.cn: protection 是这层遮盖的名词，protector 是举着它的人，protective 是能举得起它的性质。

normal.en: Unprotected adds un- to the participle, so an unprotected wire is simply a wire with no cover in front of it.
normal.cn: unprotected 在分词前加 un-，所以 unprotected wire 就是前面没有任何遮盖的电线。

normal.en: Protect looks like prove because both begin with pro-, but prove goes back to probare, to test, and has no cover in it at all.
normal.cn: protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），里面根本没有「盖住」这层意思。

abstract.en: A cover only works while it stays on the side facing the danger, which is why protection is always directed outward.
abstract.cn: 遮盖只有留在朝向危险的那一侧才有效，所以保护总是指向外面。

abstract.en: One verb holds a child, a blade, a tenant and a file because all four can be harmed by something arriving from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能护住孩子、刀身、租客和文件，因为这四者都可能被从外面来的东西伤到。

abstract.en: To protect is to lend something of your own, a coat, a law or a password, to stand between another person and harm.
abstract.cn: 保护就是把自己的一件东西——外套、法律或密码——借出去，挡在别人与伤害之间。

examples.en: She held her coat over the boy to protect him from the downpour.
examples.cn: 她把外套罩在男孩头上，替他挡住倾盆大雨。

examples.en: These rules protect tenants from sudden eviction.
examples.cn: 这些规定保障租客不被突然赶走。

examples.en: The folder was protected with a password.
examples.cn: 那个文件夹已用密码保护。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑坦克」——读音近似「扑-坦克」，人扑过去挡在坦克前面，只为护住身后的人；记住 protect 是保护。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前面）+ tegere（盖、遮）→ protegere（在前面遮住、护住）→ protectus（被护住的），十五世纪进入英语。同族词 detect（de- 去掉 + tegere 盖，即揭开盖子）、tegument（覆盖物）都保留「盖」的画面。注意 protect 与 prove 都以 pro- 开头，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验、证实），两者只是前缀相同，词根完全不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a cover held on the front side; the senses spread from shielding a body to blocking invisible threats, to legal guarantees, and finally to a password at the door of a file.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「挡在正面的那层遮盖」；义项从护住身体，扩展到拦住看不见的危险，再到法律保障，最后到文件门口的那道密码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat spread wide in front of a child while the rain hits the fabric.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件外套在孩子身前撑开，雨点全打在那层布上。

branches.en: a coat held up against the rain
branches.cn: 外套撑起来挡雨

branches.en: oil spread thin over the blade
branches.cn: 薄油涂在刀身上

branches.en: a lease clause standing between a tenant and the street
branches.cn: 一纸租约条款挡在租客与街头之间

branches.en: a password box waiting at the folder door
branches.cn: 文件夹门口等着的密码框

branches.en: one word for a coat and for a law
branches.cn: 同一个词既指外套，也指法律

intro.en: A Latin verb of covering, a prefix that moves it to the front, and two English endings that make the noun and the adjective hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示覆盖的拉丁动词、把它推到前面的前缀，以及造出名词与形容词的两个英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Tegere and protegere with their participles are the reliable Latin cognates, and the bare root teg- still shows in detect and tegument.
latinIntro.cn: tegere、protegere 及其分词是可靠的同源词；光秃秃的词根 teg- 至今还能在 detect 与 tegument 里看到。

definition_en: the state or act of being kept safe from harm, or a measure that keeps something safe
core_image: 一把撑开的伞把雨挡在头顶之外，伞骨下是一小片干的区域
scene: 举报人担心遭到报复，于是向监察机构求助。The new law offers protection for whistle-blowers who report waste.
sceneCN: 这里 protection 指「法律提供的保护措施」（第 2 个义项：由制度或规则提供的安全保障，使某人免受伤害或报复）；句意为新法律为举报浪费行为的吹哨人提供保护。图中可辨识物件：法律文本、举报信封、监察机构门牌、撑开的伞；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Physical shielding from harm
senses.definition: the state of being covered or guarded so that harm cannot reach
senses.definitionCN: 被覆盖或看守、使伤害无法到达的状态
senses.example: The umbrella offered little protection against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 那把伞对风几乎起不到防护作用。
senses.why: The Latin noun named a covering; the modern sense keeps that image of something placed between a person and a threat.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词命名一层遮盖；现代义保留「把某物置于人与威胁之间」的意象。

senses.title: Legal or institutional safeguard
senses.definition: a rule, law or arrangement that keeps a person or group safe from harm or retaliation
senses.definitionCN: 使个人或群体免受伤害或报复的规则、法律或安排
senses.example: The new law offers protection for whistle-blowers who report waste.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律为举报浪费行为的吹哨人提供保护。
senses.why: The law takes the place of the umbrella and stands between a person and a threat.
senses.whyCN: 法律替代雨伞，立在人与其威胁之间。

senses.title: Environmental conservation
senses.definition: measures taken to keep ecosystems, species or resources from damage
senses.definitionCN: 为防止生态系统、物种或资源受损而采取的措施
senses.example: The reserve was created for the protection of nesting turtles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个保护区是为保护筑巢海龟而设立的。
senses.why: Nature cannot hold an umbrella, so a reserve is built around it.
senses.whyCN: 自然无法自己撑伞，于是围绕它建立保护区。

senses.title: Social security against hardship
senses.definition: public arrangements that shield people from poverty, illness or unemployment
senses.definitionCN: 使人们免受贫困、疾病或失业的公共安排
senses.example: Social protection kept the family afloat after the layoff.
senses.exampleCN: 失业后，社会保障让这个家庭撑了下来。
senses.why: Hardship is a threat, so public arrangements are built as a cover.
senses.whyCN: 困境是一种威胁，于是公共安排被搭成遮盖。

senses.title: Safeguarding of personal data
senses.definition: rules and technical measures that keep personal information from misuse
senses.definitionCN: 防止个人信息被滥用的规则与技术措施
senses.example: Data protection requires consent before sharing.
senses.exampleCN: 数据保护要求在共享前取得同意。
senses.why: Information can be harmed, so rules form a layer around it.
senses.whyCN: 信息会受损，于是规则在它周围形成一层。

senses.title: Trade protection for domestic producers
senses.titleCN: 对本国生产者的贸易保护
senses.definition: tariffs or quotas that shield local industries from foreign competition
senses.definitionCN: 使本地产业免受外国竞争的关税或配额
senses.example: The minister argued for temporary protection of the steel sector.
senses.exampleCN: 部长主张对钢铁行业实行临时保护。
senses.why: A market under foreign competition is shielded like a town under attack.
senses.whyCN: 面对外国竞争的市场像受攻击的城镇一样被遮蔽。

senses.title: A protected area
senses.definition: a place legally set aside where wildlife or a site is shielded from development
senses.definitionCN: 依法划出、使野生动物或遗址免受开发的地方
senses.example: The reef is a marine protection where anchoring is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片珊瑚礁是一处禁止下锚的海洋保护区。
senses.why: When protection is fixed to a place, the abstract noun becomes a mapped area.
senses.whyCN: 当保护固定在某个地点，抽象名词就变成地图上的区域。

senses.title: Gear worn against injury
senses.definition: equipment worn to absorb impact or prevent injury in sport or work
senses.definitionCN: 在运动或工作中吸收冲击、防止受伤的装备
senses.example: Knee protection is compulsory on the course.
senses.exampleCN: 这条赛道上必须佩戴护膝。
senses.why: Padding is the umbrella worn on the body.
senses.whyCN: 护具是穿在身上的伞。

intro.en: Protection comes from Latin protectio 'a covering, defence', from protegere 'to cover in front', through French protection. The word is recorded in English from the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: protection 经法语 protection 来自拉丁 protectio「遮盖、防御」，后者出自 protegere「在前面遮盖」。英语自 14 世纪有记录。

items.en: Tegere 'to cover' gives the family its core image of a roof or shield over something.
items.cn: tegere「覆盖」给该词族提供核心意象：某物上方的屋顶或盾牌。

items.en: Protegere 'to cover in front, shield' added pro- 'before' to tegere.
items.cn: protegere「在前面遮盖、屏蔽」在 tegere 前加上 pro-「在前」。

items.en: Protectio named the covering or the act of shielding; its stem supplies protection and protector.
items.cn: protectio 命名遮盖或屏蔽行为；其词干提供 protection 与 protector。

items.en: Old French protection passed into English in the 1300s, first in legal and military contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 protection 于 14 世纪进入英语，最初用于法律与军事语境。

items.en: Environmental, data and social protection are nineteenth- and twentieth-century extensions of the legal sense.
items.cn: 环境、数据与社会保护是 19、20 世纪从法律义延伸出来的用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use is not precisely dated and the fourteenth-century figure is approximate. The Latin protegere and protectio layers are secure.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语使用没有精确年代，14 世纪之数为约数；拉丁 protegere 与 protectio 这两层可靠。

note.en: Group one separates the noun from the verb, adjective and agent of the family; group two separates forms of safeguarding by scope.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与同族动词、形容词、施动者；第二组按范围区分各类保障。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a guarding quality; protection is the thing provided.
entries.definitionCN: 描述防护性质的形容词；protection 是被提供的东西。

entries.definition: One who or that which protects; protection is the state or measure, not the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护者或防护装置；protection 是状态或措施，不是施动者。

entries.definition: The action of shielding; protection is the resulting state or the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指屏蔽动作；protection 是结果状态或安排。

entries.definition: Specific safeguards, as in legal protections; the singular is usually the general state.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体保障措施，如法律保护条款；单数多为一般状态。

entries.definition: Resistance to a specific attack; protection is broader and includes prevention and care.
entries.definitionCN: 指对具体攻击的抵抗；protection 更宽，包含预防与照料。

entries.definition: The condition of being safe; protection is the measure that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指安全的状态；protection 是产生该状态的措施。

entries.definition: Careful management to prevent loss of natural or cultural resources; it is one form of protection.
entries.definitionCN: 指防止自然或文化资源流失的谨慎管理；是保护的一种形式。

entries.definition: Keeping a person in official care; protection can be legal without detention.
entries.definitionCN: 指由官方照管某人；protection 可以是法律性的而不涉及拘留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin noun of covering, the real family, and the collocations of law, environment and data.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「遮盖」名词、真实词族，以及法律、环境与数据领域的固定搭配。

normal.en: protegere 'cover in front' + -ion: the state of being covered.
normal.cn: protegere「在前面遮盖」+ -ion：被遮盖的状态。

normal.en: The family runs protect, protection, protective, protector, protectionism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 protect、protection、protective、protector、protectionism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: environmental protection, data protection, legal protection.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 environmental protection、data protection、legal protection。

normal.en: The noun is countable when it means specific measures.
normal.cn: 指具体措施时，这个名词可数。

normal.en: One umbrella covers rain, law, reefs and knees.
normal.cn: 一把伞同时覆盖雨、法律、珊瑚礁与膝盖。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella holding a dry circle open in a downpour.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞在暴雨中撑开一小片干燥的圆。

abstract.en: Picture a statute standing between a witness and a threat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法规立在证人与威胁之间。

abstract.en: Picture a reef marked off by buoys so that no anchor can fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一片珊瑚礁被浮标圈起，任何锚都落不下去。

examples.en: The helmet gives reliable protection against a fall.
examples.cn: 头盔能在摔倒时提供可靠的保护。

examples.en: The park was declared a protection for the last wild herd.
examples.cn: 这座公园被宣布为最后一群野生兽群的保护区。

examples.en: Consumer protection laws require clear labelling.
examples.cn: 消费者保护法要求标示清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「protect（保护）+ -ion（状态）」——被护住的状态 → 保护；防护

root: 拉丁 pro-「在前」+ tegere「覆盖」→ protegere「在前面遮盖」→ protectio「遮盖、防御」→ 法语 protection → 英语 protection。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one umbrella: rain over a head, law over a witness, rules over a reef, welfare over a family, consent over data, a tariff over a mill, a reserve over turtles, and padding over a knee.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一把伞：替头顶挡雨、替证人挡法外报复、替珊瑚礁挡开发、替家庭挡困境、替数据挡滥用、替工厂挡竞争、替海龟挡侵扰、替膝盖挡冲击。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open umbrella holding a small dry circle inside a downpour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把撑开的伞在暴雨中守住一小片干燥的圆。

branches.en: PHYSICAL COVER: umbrellas, helmets and padding take the blow.
branches.cn: 物理遮盖：伞、头盔与护具承受冲击。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL COVER: law, welfare and consent rules stand in for the umbrella.
branches.cn: 制度遮盖：法律、福利与同意规则替代雨伞。

branches.en: CONSERVATION: measures that keep ecosystems from damage.
branches.cn: 保护措施：防止生态系统受损的行动。

branches.en: TRADE COVER: tariffs shield producers from competition.
branches.cn: 贸易遮盖：关税使生产者免受竞争。

branches.en: PLACE: protection becomes a bounded area on a map.
branches.cn: 地点：保护变成地图上一块有边界的地方。

intro.en: Protection is a Latin action noun in -io built on the protegere stem; English adds further suffixes for agent, quality and doctrine.
intro.cn: protection 是由 protegere 词干加 -io 构成的拉丁动作名词；英语再加后缀表示施动者、性质与主义。

latinIntro.en: Latin protegere, protectio and tectus carry the covering image into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protegere、protectio 与 tectus 把「遮盖」意象带入英语。

items.example: Protection from the sun matters at noon.
The treaty made the state a protector.
items.exampleCN: 条约使该国成为保护者。

items.meaning: a policy of shielding domestic industry
items.exampleCN: 保护主义抬高国内价格。

items.meaning: one who favours such a policy
items.exampleCN: 那名保护主义者阻挠了条约。

items.example: Environmental protection is written into the charter.

items.exampleCN: 数据保护规则限制共享。

items.meaning: a legal order to keep someone safe
items.meaningCN: 保护某人安全的法院命令
items.example: A protection order was served that night.
items.exampleCN: 当晚送达了一份保护令。

definition_zh: 证明；证实；结果是；检验；证明自己
definition_en: to show that something is true by evidence, to turn out to be a particular way, or to test something in practice
core_image: 一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停了下来
scene: 争论一直持续到深夜，直到有人把当年的登记簿翻到那一页，指着上面的签名。The old register proved that the land had belonged to her family.
sceneCN: 这里表示「证明、证实」（第 1 个义项：用证据使某件事确定为真）；句意为那本旧登记簿证明了这块地一直属于她家。

derivatives.zh: 与 prove 同源的名词，经古法语 preove 而来，义为「证据；证明」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被证实的；经考验的」
由 prove 加 -able 构成，义为「可证明的」
由 prove 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「证明……有误；驳倒」

senses.title: To show that something is true
senses.definition: to give facts, documents or tests that make it certain that something is true or real
senses.definitionCN: 拿出事实、文件或检验，使某事被确定为真或确实存在
senses.example: The fingerprints proved that he had been in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 指纹证明他曾在那间屋子里。
senses.why: Latin probare meant to test something and find it good, so proving starts as an examination that ends in a verdict rather than as a mere opinion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验某物并认定它站得住，所以「证明」起初是一场检验，最后落成判决，而不只是看法。

senses.title: To turn out to be a particular thing
senses.definition: to be found, after events have unfolded, to have a certain quality, often one that was not expected
senses.definitionCN: 事情展开之后，被发现具有某种性质，且常是原先没料到的
senses.example: The shortcut proved longer than the road we usually take.
senses.exampleCN: 那条近路结果比我们常走的路还远。
senses.why: Once a test is finished, the result simply is what it is; English lets the verb carry that outcome, so a thing can prove difficult without anyone proving it.
senses.whyCN: 检验结束之后，结果就摆在那里；英语让这个动词直接承担结果，于是事物本身可以 prove difficult，而不需要谁去证明它。

senses.title: To test something in order to learn its quality
senses.definition: to try a method, a weapon or a machine under real conditions to see whether it works
senses.definitionCN: 在真实条件下试用某种方法、武器或机器，看它是否管用
senses.example: The engineers proved the new pump under heavy load before selling it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在重载下检验了新水泵，然后才出售。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer made visible: before a thing can be proved true, it has to be put to the test, and the verb still names that trial.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老那层意思的直接显现：在被证明为真之前，东西得先经受检验，而这个动词至今仍指那场试验。

senses.title: To show one's own ability or courage
senses.definition: to show through action that one deserves a place, a role or respect
senses.definitionCN: 通过行动表明自己配得上某个位置、角色或尊重
senses.example: She proved herself in her first month on the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她在上夜班的第一个月就证明了自己。
senses.why: When the thing being proved is the speaker, the test and the result collapse into one act, which is why English says prove oneself rather than adding true as well.
senses.whyCN: 当被证明的对象是说话者本人时，检验与结果合成一个动作，所以英语说 prove oneself，不再额外加 true。

intro.en: Prove descends from a Latin verb that meant to test and to judge as good; English keeps both the trial and the verdict, and later let the word also mean to turn out.
intro.cn: prove 源自一个意为「检验并判定为好」的拉丁动词；英语同时保留了检验与判决，后来又让它表示「结果如何」。

items.en: Probus meant upright, honest and of good quality, said of a person or a thing that had been checked.
items.cn: probus 意为正直、诚实、品质良好，用于经过查验的人或物。

items.en: Probare meant to test something and to approve it as good, joining the act of examining to the verdict.
items.cn: probare 意为检验某物并认可它合格，把查验的动作与判决连在一起。

items.en: The participle probatus described what had stood the test, and it is the shape behind the English word.
items.cn: 分词 probatus 描述经住了检验的东西，是英语这个词背后的形式。

items.en: Old French prover meant to test and to demonstrate, and it brought the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 prover 意为检验、论证，把这个动词带进英语。

items.en: English split the old family: proof became the noun for the evidence, while prove kept the testing and added the modern sense of turning out.
items.cn: 英语把这一族拆开：proof 成为表示证据的名词，prove 留住检验，又添上「结果是」这层现代用法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of testing, including the noun English split off from it; the second group gathers verbs for showing something to be true or false.
note.cn: 第一组共用表示「检验」的拉丁动词，包括英语从它分出去的名词；第二组收表示「表明真假」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for evidence that settles a question, split off from the same French form.
entries.definitionCN: 能定下疑问的证据名词，与动词同出法语形式。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something already shown to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作形容词，指已被证实的东西。

entries.definition: Likely to be true, from the same Latin verb of testing and approving.
entries.definitionCN: 很可能是真的，出自同一个表示检验与认可的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To investigate closely, originally to test a wound or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查究，原指探查伤口或表面。

entries.definition: To show clearly by argument or by an example.
entries.definitionCN: 用论证或实例清楚地表明。

entries.definition: To check that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否真实、准确。

entries.definition: To show that a fact is certain, often in a formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某事实确凿，常较正式。

entries.definition: To be discovered to be a particular way in the end.
entries.definitionCN: 最终被发现是某种样子。

normalIntro.en: The family keeps the picture of a test that ends in a verdict: something is put under pressure, and the result is then allowed to speak.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词保留着「检验之后落成判决」的画面：某物被压上压力，然后让结果自己说话。

normal.en: Probare is to test and to approve, so prove carries a courtroom inside it: first the examination, then the finding.
normal.cn: probare 既是检验也是认可，所以 prove 里装着一间法庭：先审，再判。

normal.en: Proof is the same family seen as a thing rather than an act, which is why a proof is handed over while a prove is performed.
normal.cn: proof 是同一族词被看成「物」而不是「动作」，所以 proof 可以递过去，prove 只能被执行。

normal.en: Probable keeps the approving half: what is probable has enough testing behind it to be believed.
normal.cn: probable 保留了「认可」的那一半：很可能的事，背后已有足够的检验让人相信。

normal.en: Disprove adds dis- to the front, so the test now ends in rejection instead of approval.
normal.cn: disprove 在前面加 dis-，于是检验以否定而不是认可收场。

normal.en: Prove looks like protect because both start with pro-, but probare means to test, and there is no covering anywhere in it.
normal.cn: prove 与 protect 都以 pro- 开头，但 probare 意为检验，其中没有任何「遮盖」。

abstract.en: A proof is a test that has stopped being a question, and the verb marks the moment that change happens.
abstract.cn: 证据是一场不再提问的检验，而这个动词标出的正是那变化发生的瞬间。

abstract.en: One word covers testing, judging and turning out because all three are stages of the same examination.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指检验、判定与结果，因为三者是同一场查验的不同阶段。

abstract.en: To prove something is to accept that it might fail, which is why the word is as much about risk as about certainty.
abstract.cn: 证明某物，就是承认它有可能失败，所以这个词既关乎确定，也关乎冒险。

examples.en: The video proved that the door had been locked all night.
examples.cn: 录像证明那扇门整夜都锁着。

examples.en: The task proved harder than anyone expected.
examples.cn: 这项任务结果比任何人预料的都难。

examples.en: He worked two extra shifts to prove himself.
examples.cn: 他多上了两个班来证明自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普如夫」——像「扑过去捋清楚」，把乱糟糟的事捋到只剩一条真相；记住 prove 是证明。

root: 拉丁语 probus（正直的、品质良好的）→ probare（检验、验后认可）→ probatus（经住检验的），经古法语 prover 进入英语；同族词还有 proof、probable、probe、probity。注意 prove 与 protect 都带前缀 pro-，但 prove 的词根是 probare（检验），protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），两者只是前缀相同。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a test ending in a verdict; the senses run from proving a fact, through the result of events, to testing a thing and proving oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「以检验收尾的判定」；义项从证明一个事实，到事情的结果，再到检验一物与证明自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of papers pushed across a table, and a stamp on the last page that ends every doubt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料被推到桌上，最后一页的印章让所有疑问停下来。

branches.en: a register opened to the page with the signature
branches.cn: 登记簿翻到有签名的那一页

branches.en: a short cut that turns out longer
branches.cn: 结果反而更远的那条近路

branches.en: a pump running under heavy load
branches.cn: 重载下运转的水泵

branches.en: a new worker taking the hardest shift
branches.cn: 新人接下最难的班次

branches.en: one word for examining and for concluding
branches.cn: 同一个词既指查验也指结论

intro.en: A Latin adjective of good quality, the verb of testing built on it, and the French and English forms that split into proof and prove hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示品质良好的拉丁形容词、由它构成的「检验」动词，以及分化为 proof 与 prove 的法语、英语形式，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Probus, probare and probatus are the reliable Latin cognates, and proof is the same family seen as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: probus、probare 与 probatus 是可靠的同源词；proof 则是同一族词被看成名词的样子。

definition_zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；防备
definition_en: to give or supply something that is needed, to state a rule in a law or contract, or to support someone with money
core_image: 旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，再转身把干粮和水递给身后的人
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，村口的空地上支起几张长桌，志愿者把水和面包摆成一排。The relief team came to provide blankets and hot food for the flooded villages.
sceneCN: 这里取「提供、供给」的意思（第 1 个义项：把别人需要的东西给出去）；句意为救援队来为受淹的村庄提供毛毯和热食。村口长桌上摆开的水和面包就是线索。

pos.zh: 提供；供给；规定；供养；为…做准备

derivatives.zh: 由 provide 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「供应者；提供者」
由拉丁语名词 provisio（预见、照料）经法语进入英语，义为「供应；条款；储备」
由拉丁词干 provid- 加 -ent 构成，义为「有远见的；用钱谨慎的」
由过去分词转成的连词，义为「假如；只要」，常见于 provided that

senses.title: To supply something that is needed
senses.definition: to give someone something they need or to make something available for use
senses.definitionCN: 把别人需要的东西给出去，或使某物可供使用
senses.example: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。
senses.why: Latin providere joins pro-, ahead, to videre, to see; seeing ahead means noticing a need before it arrives, and the next move is to get the thing ready and hand it over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 providere 把表示「在前」的 pro- 接在 videre（看）上：提前看见，就是在需求到来之前先察觉；察觉之后最自然的动作，就是把东西备好递过去，于是「预先看见」变成了「供给」。

senses.title: To state as a rule in a law or contract
senses.definition: to establish a rule or condition in a law, contract or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、合同或协议中确立某条规则或条件
senses.example: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。
senses.why: A rule written in advance is itself a kind of foresight: the text settles now what will happen later, so the verb that means to get ready also names what a document lays down beforehand.
senses.whyCN: 提前写好的条文本身就是一种预见：文本在此刻就决定了以后会发生什么，所以那个表示「预先备好」的动词，也用来指文件事先订下的内容。

senses.title: To support someone financially
senses.definition: to earn the money that allows another person, especially a family member, to live
senses.definitionCN: 挣钱供另一个人生活，尤指供养家庭成员
senses.example: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
senses.exampleCN: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。
senses.why: Providing for someone is looking ahead on their behalf: the money is set aside before the need is felt, which is the household version of seeing ahead.
senses.whyCN: 供养一个人，就是替对方往前看：钱在需求出现之前就留出来，这正是「预先看见」在家庭里的样子。

senses.title: To make preparation against something
senses.definition: to take action in advance so that a possible problem or danger does less harm
senses.definitionCN: 提前采取行动，使可能出现的问题或危险危害更小
senses.example: They built the wall to provide against flooding in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修了这道墙，用来防备春季洪水。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is pure foresight with nothing given away: to provide against a risk is to see it coming and move before it lands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是纯粹的「预先看见」，与给东西无关：provide against 某个风险，就是看出它会来，并在它落地之前先动手。

intro.en: Provide is built from two Latin pieces meaning ahead and to see, and that single image of foresight later spreads into supply, legal rules and family support.
intro.cn: provide 由两个拉丁语成分构成，意思分别是「在前」和「看」；这一「预先看见」的画面后来扩展到供给、法律条文与养家。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it supplied the visual core of a large family of Latin words.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，为一大族拉丁词提供了「看」这个核心。

items.en: Pro- meant ahead or in front, so providere meant to see ahead, to foresee and to take care of something in advance.
items.cn: pro- 表示「在前、预先」，所以 providere 意为往前看、预见，并提前照管某事。

items.en: The noun providentia named foresight and careful management, and it survives in the English words providence and provident.
items.cn: 名词 providentia 指远见与谨慎的照料，它留在英语的 providence 与 provident 里。

items.en: Old French pourveoir kept both halves of the meaning: to foresee a need and to supply what it calls for.
items.cn: 古法语 pourveoir 保留了两半意思：既预见需求，也提供需求所需的东西。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as provide and carried the word into law, where a document provides, and into the household, where a wage provides for a family.
items.cn: 英语把拼写固定为 provide，并把这个词带进法律——文件可以「规定」，也带进家庭——工资可以「养家」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of seeing ahead; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for giving what is needed.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「预先看见」动词上的词；近义组收表示「给出所需之物」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for supplying something, and also a clause in a document.
entries.definitionCN: 表示供应之事的名字，也指文件中的条款。

entries.definition: Care or guidance that looks ahead, often attributed to a higher power.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来作准备的照管，常被归于更高的力量。

entries.definition: Careful about the future, especially with money.
entries.definitionCN: 为将来打算的，尤指用钱谨慎的。

entries.definition: A person or a company that supplies something.
entries.definitionCN: 提供某物的人或机构。

entries.definition: To give or sell what is needed over time.
entries.definitionCN: 持续提供或出售所需之物。

entries.definition: To provide furniture or whatever else is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 提供家具或所需之物。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to take.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西拿出来供人取用。

entries.definition: To supply with tools or skills for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的提供工具或技能。

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a look into the future, not with a gift, and its family keeps returning to foresight, readiness and the handover that follows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是送礼；同族词反复回到预见、准备以及随之而来的交付。

normal.en: Pro- means ahead and videre means to see, so provide begins with a look into the future rather than with an object.
normal.cn: pro- 意为「在前」，videre 意为「看」，所以 provide 的起点是往未来看一眼，而不是某件东西。

normal.en: Provision is the noun built on the same stem: what has been seen ahead and therefore got ready.
normal.cn: provision 是同一词干上的名词：预先看见、因此备好的东西。

normal.en: The legal use, as in the law provides, works because a written rule also decides the future in advance.
normal.cn: 法律用法如 the law provides 之所以成立，是因为写下的规则同样在提前决定未来。

normal.en: Provider adds -er, the person who does the providing, exactly as in employer and adviser.
normal.cn: provider 加 -er，指做「提供」这件事的人，与 employer、adviser 的构造相同。

normal.en: Provided that keeps the past participle and turns it into a condition: if this is seen to, the rest follows.
normal.cn: provided that 保留过去分词形式，把它变成条件：只要这一点被照看到，其余便随之成立。

abstract.en: To provide is to act on a future you have already seen, which is why the word sounds like care more than charity.
abstract.cn: 提供是对一个你已经看见的未来采取行动，所以这个词听起来更像照料，而不像施舍。

abstract.en: A law that provides and a parent who provides are doing one thing: fixing tomorrow before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 法律规定与父母供养做的是同一件事：在明天到来之前就把它安排下来。

abstract.en: The whole word lives in the gap between seeing a need and meeting it.
abstract.cn: 从看见需求到满足需求之间的那段距离，正是这个词的全部所在。

examples.en: The school provides free meals for children from poor families.
examples.cn: 学校为贫困家庭的孩子提供免费餐食。

examples.en: The contract provides that the rent must be paid on the first day of each month.
examples.cn: 合同规定租金须在每月第一天支付。

examples.en: He works two jobs to provide for his elderly parents.
examples.cn: 他打两份工来赡养年迈的父母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑若外德」——听着像「铺好喂的」，先把吃的用的铺好喂到人跟前，正是提供。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前、预先）+ videre（看见）构成 providere，本义「预先看到、提前照管」，由此引申为「预备、供给、规定、供养」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is foresight; the senses divide into supplying a need, writing a rule down, supporting a family, and guarding against a risk.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「预先看见」；义项分成满足需求、把规则写下来、供养家人，以及防备风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller standing on a rise, looking far down the road, then turning back to hand food and water to those behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人站上高坡，把前路看得很远，然后转身把干粮和水递给身后的人。

branches.en: a table of food laid out before anyone asks
branches.cn: 没人开口前就摆好的一桌食物

branches.en: a clause printed in small type at the end of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾用小字印出的条款

branches.en: a wage that keeps an old couple fed
branches.cn: 让一对老人吃得上饭的一份工资

branches.en: a wall raised before the river rises
branches.cn: 河水上涨之前就砌起的墙

branches.en: a store of grain kept for a bad year
branches.cn: 为荒年留下的存粮

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of seeing hold the word together, and French reshaped the verb before English took it.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示「看见」的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，法语先在中间改造了动词形式，英语随后借入。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, the compound providere, to see ahead, and the noun providentia, foresight, are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）、复合形式 providere（往前看）与名词 providentia（远见）是英语这个词的直接来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to see ahead, to take care

definition_zh: 公共的；公开的；公众的；公众；公开场合
definition_en: open for everyone to use or see, not hidden, and relating to the people as a whole; also the people themselves
core_image: 广场中央的一盏灯，四面都照得到，谁走近都能看清
scene: 广场的公告栏刚换上新的通知，路过的行人都停下来读那几行字。The council made the plan public only after every resident had been told.
sceneCN: 这里 public 是「公开的、不再保密的」（第 2 个义项）；句意为在通知到每位居民之后，市政会才把方案公开。图中可辨识物件：公告栏、通知纸、驻足的路人。

derivatives.zh: public 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「宣传；曝光度」
public 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「公开地」
同出拉丁 publicare（使公开），义为「出版；发表」
来自拉丁 res publica（公共之事），义为「共和国」
public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；使公开」

senses.title: Available for everyone to use
senses.definition: provided for all people to use, rather than for one person or a small group
senses.definitionCN: 供所有人使用，而不是供某个人或某个小圈子使用
senses.example: The public library stays open until nine.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公共图书馆开到晚上九点。
senses.why: The Latin adjective named what belonged to the people as a body, so a thing held in common rather than privately was called public.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词本指「属于人民全体的」，因此凡由众人共有、不由私人占有的东西，就被称作 public。

senses.title: Known or seen by everyone
senses.definition: known or seen by everyone, with nothing kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 所有人都知道或看见的，没有任何部分被保密
senses.example: The report became public after the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判结束后，这份报告被公开了。
senses.why: If something belongs to all the people, hiding it from them makes no sense, so shared ownership slides into shared knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然属于全体人民，瞒着他们就没有道理，于是「共有」自然滑向「共知」。

senses.title: Relating to the people or the state
senses.definition: relating to the people as a whole, or to work done by the state on their behalf
senses.definitionCN: 与全体人民有关，或与以人民名义运作的国家事务有关
senses.example: Public spending on roads fell last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年用于道路的公共开支下降了。
senses.why: Money and decisions that concern everyone are handled in the name of all, so the adjective also marks what the state holds rather than what a private owner holds.
senses.whyCN: 涉及所有人的钱和决定都以全体之名来打理，所以这个词也用来标明由国家、而非私人掌握的事物。

senses.title: The people as a whole
senses.definition: the people of a country or community considered as one body, especially as readers, viewers or voters
senses.definitionCN: 把一个国家或社区的人看作一个整体，尤指读者、观众或选民
senses.example: The gallery opened its doors to the public at ten.
senses.exampleCN: 美术馆十点向公众开门。
senses.why: The adjective was used so often with a noun left unsaid that it became a noun itself, naming the crowd a place is open to.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常与一个被省略的名词连用，久而久之自己变成了名词，专指场所向其开放的那群人。

senses.title: An open setting where others can see and hear
senses.definition: an open place or setting where other people can see and hear what happens
senses.definitionCN: 一个开放的场景，别人能看见、听见发生的事
senses.example: She has never sung in public before.
senses.exampleCN: 她以前从未在公开场合唱过歌。
senses.why: A public place is one open to all, so the noun in the phrase in public names that open setting itself, in contrast with a private room.
senses.whyCN: public 的地方就是对所有人开放的地方，因此 in public 中的名词正指这个开放场景本身，与私密房间相对。

intro.en: Public came into English through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people; the noun use is a later English development.
intro.cn: public 经法语从拉丁语 publicus 进入英语，publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词；名词用法是英语后来发展出来的。

items.en: Populus meant the people as a body, and it is the base from which publicus was formed.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是构成 publicus 的基础。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state; an older form poplicus is recorded, which shows the link with populus.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」；文献中还有更早的形式 poplicus，可见它与 populus 的联系。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as public with the same sense of open and common, and passed it into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 public，保留「开放的、共有的」意思，十五世纪传入英语。

items.en: English began using public as a noun for the people, first in phrases such as in public and then standing alone with the definite article.
items.cn: 英语开始把 public 用作指人民的名词，先出现在 in public 这类短语中，后来能单独与定冠词连用。

items.en: Modern English builds public transport, public health and public opinion, and pairs public with private as opposite poles.
items.cn: 现代英语构成 public transport、public health、public opinion 等说法，并把 public 与 private 配成对立的两极。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers English words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is shared or open.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一拉丁词干上的英语词；近义组收表示「共有、开放」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for attention from the media, formed with -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ity 构成、指媒体关注的名词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public, from Latin publicare.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行，出自拉丁语 publicare。

entries.definition: A state whose head is elected, from Latin res publica, the public thing.
entries.definitionCN: 元首经选举产生的国家，出自拉丁语 res publica（公共之事）。

entries.definition: A British pub keeper; the Latin word meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英国的酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原指包税人。

entries.definition: Shared by a group rather than owned by one person.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共用，而非一人独占的。

entries.definition: Done or held by all the members of a group together.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体全体成员共同做出或持有的。

entries.definition: Not closed or hidden, and free for anyone to enter.
entries.definitionCN: 未关闭、未隐藏，任何人都可进入的。

entries.definition: Relating to a town and the duties of the people who live there.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇及居民义务有关的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people, and English later let it stand alone as a noun for those people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词，英语后来让它单独作名词，指那些人民。

normal.en: Public came through French from Latin publicus, an adjective built on populus, the people.
normal.cn: public 经法语来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 是由 populus（人民）构成的形容词。

normal.en: The noun public is the adjective standing alone, naming the people a place is open to.
normal.cn: 名词 public 就是单独站立的形容词，指场所向其开放的那群人。

normal.en: Public and private form a pair: one belongs to all, the other belongs to one person or one household.
normal.cn: public 与 private 成对：前者属于所有人，后者属于一个人或一个家庭。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity and publicly is public with -ly, and both keep the same idea of openness.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，publicly 是 public 加 -ly，两者都保留着同一层「开放」的意思。

normal.en: Publish comes from Latin publicare, to make public, which is why publishing is always an act aimed at readers.
normal.cn: publish 出自拉丁 publicare（使公开），所以出版始终是朝着读者做出的动作。

abstract.en: The word is a lamp in the middle of a square: no side of the square is darker than another.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是广场中央的一盏灯：广场的任何一边都不会比另一边更暗。

abstract.en: A matter turns public when the cost of hiding it grows higher than the cost of showing it.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以转为公开，往往是因为隐瞒的代价高过了示人的代价。

abstract.en: English keeps one word for shared ownership, shared knowledge and shared space, as if all three were one openness.
abstract.cn: 英语用同一个词涵盖共有、共知与共用空间，仿佛这三者本就是同一种开放。

examples.en: The park is public land, so anyone may walk there.
examples.cn: 这座公园是公共土地，任何人都可以进去散步。

examples.en: Details of the deal were made public yesterday.
examples.cn: 交易的细节昨天被公开了。

examples.en: He rarely speaks in public.
examples.cn: 他很少在公开场合讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布立克」——广场上人人都立着看得见，记住 public 是公共的、公开的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（人民）→ publicus（属于人民的）→ 古法语 public → 英语 public；加 -ity 得 publicity，加 -ly 得 publicly，词义核心都是「向所有人开放」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to all the people; the senses divide into shared use, shared knowledge, state affairs, the people themselves, and the open setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于全体人民的东西」；义项由此分为共同使用、共同知晓、国家事务、人民本身，以及开放的场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp at the centre of a square, lighting every side of it evenly.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场正中的一盏灯，把四面照得一样亮。

branches.en: a library door with no ticket desk
branches.cn: 没有售票台的图书馆大门

branches.en: a lamp that leaves no corner dark
branches.cn: 一盏不留下暗角的灯

branches.en: a road paid for out of common funds
branches.cn: 用公共资金修起来的路

branches.en: a crowd waiting for the gallery to open
branches.cn: 等着美术馆开门的人群

branches.en: a first song sung before strangers
branches.cn: 第一次在陌生人面前唱歌

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective built on it, and the English endings -ity and -ly that turn it into a noun and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词，以及把它变成名词与副词的英语后缀 -ity、-ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 公开性；公众所知的状态

definition_zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤；拉力；吸引力；影响力
definition_en: to move something towards oneself or in a stated direction by using force; to remove something by drawing it out; to injure a muscle; also the force that draws, a physical attraction, and personal influence
core_image: 一个人双手攥住粗绳，脚蹬地面，把绳子一点点拽向自己
scene: 绳子另一头卡在石缝里，几个人排成一列，脚掌抵住地面，一起把劲儿往后使。They pulled the rope until the log slid out of the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 pull 是「拉、拽」（第 1 个义项：用力把东西朝自己或某个方向移动）；句意为他们一直拉绳子，直到那根木头从泥里滑出来。图中可辨识物件：粗绳、石缝、蹬地的脚。

derivatives.zh: pull 与 over 复合，指从头上套下去穿的毛衣
pull 与 back 复合，指军队或企业的撤退、收缩
pull 加表人后缀 -er，指拉东西的人或拔取工具

senses.title: To move something towards oneself
senses.definition: to move a person or thing towards oneself or along behind oneself by using force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把人或物朝自己方向移动，或让其在身后跟着移动
senses.example: She pulled the heavy box across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那个沉重的箱子拖着在地板上移动。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to pluck or tug at something, so the body's grip and the backward motion are both built into the word from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「揪、拽」，所以手握住的力道和向后移动的方向从一开始就长在词里。

senses.title: To remove something by drawing it out
senses.definition: to take something out of a place or a body by drawing it steadily away
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续往外拽，把某物从某个位置或身体里取出来
senses.example: The dentist pulled two of his teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医拔掉了他两颗牙。
senses.why: Pulling in the first sense moves a whole object; aim the same motion at a part held inside something and the meaning narrows to extraction.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的拉是移动整个物体；把同样的动作对准嵌在某物内部的东西，词义就收窄为「拔出」。

senses.title: To injure a muscle by overstretching it
senses.definition: to damage a muscle or tendon by stretching it too far
senses.definitionCN: 因拉伸过度而损伤肌肉或肌腱
senses.example: He pulled a muscle in his calf during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在短跑时拉伤了小腿肌肉。
senses.why: The fibres of a muscle are drawn apart by a sudden load, and English describes that damage with the same verb it uses for drawing something apart.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉纤维被突然的负荷拽开，英语就用「往开拽」这个动词来描述这种损伤。

senses.title: A steady force that draws something
senses.definition: a force that draws an object steadily in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 把物体持续朝某个方向吸引的力
senses.example: The pull of the moon lifts the sea into tides.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力把海水拉起，形成潮汐。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the force behind it, so a rope, a magnet and the moon all exert a pull.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指这个动作，名词就能指动作背后的力，于是绳子、磁铁和月亮都能产生 pull。

senses.title: Personal influence or attraction
senses.definition: the power to influence events or attract people, especially through connections
senses.definitionCN: 影响事情或吸引他人的力量，尤指凭借人脉关系
senses.example: His family has a lot of pull in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在这个镇上很有门路。
senses.why: A person with connections can draw decisions the way a rope draws a load, so the physical sense extends to social leverage and charm.
senses.whyCN: 有门路的人能像绳子拉动货物那样牵动决定，于是物理义延伸到社会上的影响力与魅力。

intro.en: Pull is an Old English verb of Germanic stock, first recorded as pullian with the sense of plucking or tugging; it has no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pull 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语动词，最早写作 pullian，意为「揪、拽」；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: Pullian is recorded in Old English with the sense of plucking wool or tugging at something, and it already implies a hand closing on a thing.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pullian 意为揪羊毛、拽东西，词里已经含有「手攥住某物」的意思。

items.en: The verb belongs to the Germanic layer of English rather than to the Latin layer, and related forms appear in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个动词属于英语的日耳曼语层而非拉丁语层，在几种日耳曼语言中都有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and widened it from plucking to any steady drawing motion, including pulling a cart or a rope.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并把词义从「揪」扩大到任何持续拖拽的动作，包括拉车、拉绳。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun pull appears beside the verb, naming the act and later the force itself.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，名词 pull 出现在动词旁边，先指拉这个动作，后来指拉力本身。

items.en: Modern English uses pull for drawing, extracting, straining a muscle, physical attraction, and social influence, and keeps it in dozens of phrasal verbs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pull 表示拉、拔出、拉伤肌肉、物理吸引与社会影响力，并让它出现在大量短语动词中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ from pull by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pull 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「用力移动某物」的动词。

entries.definition: A small area of still water, or a shared fund of money.
entries.definitionCN: 一小片静水，或共同凑集的一笔钱。

entries.definition: The adult male of cattle.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的公牛。

entries.definition: The soft wet mass of crushed fruit or paper fibre.
entries.definitionCN: 压碎的水果或纸纤维形成的软浆。

entries.definition: A cloth spread over a coffin, or a gloom that settles on a place.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖棺木的布，或笼罩某地的阴郁气氛。

entries.definition: To pull something heavy along a surface with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把沉重的东西沿地面拉动。

entries.definition: To pull something sharply and briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地、短暂地拉一下。

entries.definition: To pull or carry something heavy over a distance.
entries.definitionCN: 把沉重的东西拖拉或搬运一段距离。

entries.definition: To pull something with a sudden hard movement.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地一拽。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic verb for closing a hand on something and drawing it back, and its family keeps that backward motion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼动词，指手攥住东西往后拽，它的同族词都保留着这股向后的力道。

normal.en: Pull goes back to Old English pullian, to pluck or tug, and it never needed a Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: pull 上溯到古英语 pullian（揪、拽），它从来不需要一个拉丁祖先。

normal.en: Pull out, pull up and pull over are phrasal verbs: the particle tells you which direction the drawing goes.
normal.cn: pull out、pull up、pull over 都是短语动词，小品词告诉你拉力朝哪个方向。

normal.en: Pull a muscle is the same motion turned inward, because the fibres are drawn apart inside the leg.
normal.cn: pull a muscle 是把同一个动作转向身体内部，因为腿里的纤维被拽开了。

normal.en: Pullover is a garment you pull over your head, so the compound keeps the original gesture in plain sight.
normal.cn: pullover 是从头上拉下去穿的衣服，复合词把原来的动作明明白白留在里面。

normal.en: The noun pull can mean influence, because a person who can draw decisions is doing what a rope does to a load.
normal.cn: 名词 pull 能指影响力，因为能牵动决定的人，做的正是绳子对货物做的事。

abstract.en: A pull is a relationship: something on one end always answers to something on the other.
abstract.cn: 拉是一种关系：一端的东西总是在回应另一端。

abstract.en: English lets one short verb cover rope, tooth, muscle and reputation, because all four resist and then give way.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个短动词同时覆盖绳子、牙齿、肌肉和名声，因为这四样都会先抵抗、然后松脱。

abstract.en: What draws a person is not so different from what draws a boat: a force outside, and a rope that holds.
abstract.cn: 吸引一个人的力量和拉动一条船的力量相差不大：外面一股力，中间一根绳。

examples.en: He pulled the chair closer to the fire.
examples.cn: 他把椅子拉近火边。

examples.en: The nurse pulled the sheet back to check the wound.
examples.cn: 护士把床单拉开查看伤口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑」——人往前一扑，抓住东西就往回拽，记住 pull 是拉。

root: 古英语 pullian（揪、拽），属日耳曼语层，无可靠拉丁同族词；由「手攥住往后拽」这一动作，发展出拔出、拉伤、拉力、吸引力与影响力诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand closing on something and drawing it back; the senses divide into moving a whole object, extracting a part, straining a muscle, the force itself, and social leverage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手攥住东西往回拽」；义项由此分为移动整个物体、取出其中一部分、拉伤肌肉、力本身，以及社会上的影响力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a thick rope, feet braced on the ground, drawing it back inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手攥住粗绳，双脚蹬地，一寸寸把绳子拽回来。

branches.en: a door dragged open against a stiff hinge

definition_zh: 惩罚；处罚；严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏；重创（对手）；猛烈抨击；使身体极度疲惫
definition_en: to make someone suffer for a wrong, or to treat a person or thing so harshly that it is worn down
core_image: 木槌落下，犯错的人被带离座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛
scene: 夜间巡查时，看守发现一名囚犯试图翻墙逃走，于是把他单独关进一间没有窗的小屋。The warden punished the prisoner by locking him alone in a windowless cell.
sceneCN: 这里指「因过错而使某人受苦」，对应第 1 个义项：让犯错者为自己的行为承担痛苦；句意为看守把企图逃跑的囚犯单独关进没有窗的小屋作为惩罚。画面要点：夜间走廊、翻墙的脚印、被关上的铁门；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（及物动词，常与 for 连用说明过错）
严厉对待；粗暴使用使损坏（口语中可指物）

forms.label: 现在分词作形容词（折磨人的）

derivatives.zh: 由 punish 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作结果）→ 由「使人受苦这一动作」转为「所施加的那份痛苦或处罚」
由 punish 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表能够被）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「依法可以受罚的」
由 punish 加现在分词后缀 → 由「惩罚他人」转为形容「像惩罚一样消耗人的、折磨人的」
由 punish 加施事后缀（表施动者）→ 由「惩罚」这一动作转为「施加惩罚的那个人」
与 punish 同出拉丁 punire，加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「施加惩罚」转为「以惩罚为目的的、惩罚性的」
与 punish 同出拉丁 poena，经古法语形成名词 → 由「惩罚这一动作」转为「作为惩罚所付的那笔代价」

senses.title: To make someone suffer for a wrong
senses.definition: to cause a person who has done wrong to undergo pain, loss or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 使做错事的人经历痛苦、损失或艰难
senses.example: The company punished the clerk for leaking the file.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因那名职员泄露文件而惩罚了他。
senses.why: Latin punire meant to make someone pay for a wrong, so the core idea is not pain for its own sake but a debt being settled through suffering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 punire 意为让某人为过错付出代价，所以核心并不是疼痛本身，而是一笔债通过受苦被结清。

senses.title: To sentence in a court
senses.definition: to impose a legal sentence on a convicted person
senses.definitionCN: 对已被定罪的人施加法律判决
senses.example: The court punished the fraud with five years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭判处那名诈骗犯五年监禁。
senses.why: When the debt is collected by a court, the suffering is fixed by law, given a name and given a term.
senses.whyCN: 当这笔债由法庭来收取，痛苦就由法律确定，被赋予名称，也被赋予期限。

senses.title: To discipline a child or pupil
senses.definition: to correct a child or pupil by withdrawing something valued or by mild suffering
senses.definitionCN: 以收回孩子看重的某物或轻微的苦头来纠正其行为
senses.example: His parents punished him by cancelling the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他父母取消旅行作为对他的惩罚。
senses.why: A household collects the same debt in miniature: a small wrong, a small withdrawal of what the child values.
senses.whyCN: 家庭以缩小的尺度收取同一笔债：小小的过错，配上小小地拿走孩子看重的东西。

senses.title: To treat someone with deliberate harshness
senses.titleCN: 刻意以严酷手段对待某人
senses.definition: to subject a person to prolonged harsh treatment, whether or not a rule was broken
senses.definitionCN: 使某人长时间承受严酷对待，不论是否真的违规
senses.example: The guards punished the prisoners by keeping them standing all night.
senses.exampleCN: 看守让囚犯整夜站立，以此折磨他们。
senses.why: Once pain is separated from the debt, any deliberate infliction of suffering can take the name, even where no rule exists to be broken.
senses.whyCN: 一旦疼痛与那笔债脱钩，任何刻意施加的痛苦都能叫这个名字，哪怕并不存在可供违反的规则。

senses.title: To damage something by rough use
senses.titleCN: 因粗暴使用而损坏某物
senses.definition: to wear out or damage an object by using it far harder than it was designed for
senses.definitionCN: 以远超设计承受的方式使用，使物品磨损或损坏
senses.example: Rough roads punish the tyres far more than smooth ones.
senses.exampleCN: 崎岖路面比平坦路面更伤轮胎。
senses.why: Objects cannot owe a debt, so the word transfers to rough treatment that makes a thing suffer wear, as if the thing were being made to pay.
senses.whyCN: 物品不可能欠债，于是这个词转到「粗暴对待使某物受损」上，仿佛那件东西也在被逼着付出代价。

senses.title: To defeat an opponent by a wide margin
senses.titleCN: 以压倒性优势重创对手
senses.definition: to beat an opponent so heavily that the defeat feels like a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 以极大差距击败对手，使这场失败如同一种惩罚
senses.example: The champions punished the visitors with four goals in twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军队在二十分钟内连进四球，重创了客队。
senses.why: A contest can turn a score into a debt, and a heavy defeat is that debt being collected all at once.
senses.whyCN: 比赛可以把比分变成一笔债，而一场惨败就是这笔债被一次性收走。

senses.title: To criticise sharply
senses.definition: to attack a person, work or idea with very severe public criticism
senses.definitionCN: 以极严厉的公开批评攻击某人、某作品或某观点
senses.example: The critics punished the film for its empty spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人猛烈抨击这部影片空洞的视觉堆砌。
senses.why: Words can inflict suffering too, so sharp criticism borrows the same verb and makes its target pay in reputation.
senses.whyCN: 言语也能造成痛苦，于是尖锐的批评借用了同一个动词，让对象以名声偿付。

senses.title: To exhaust the body through effort
senses.titleCN: 使身体因用力而极度疲惫
senses.definition: to strain the body so hard that the effort feels like a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 使身体承担极大负荷，让这种用力如同惩罚
senses.example: The steep climb punished legs that had not trained.
senses.exampleCN: 陡峭的山路让未经训练的腿吃尽苦头。
senses.why: The body itself can be made to pay for the effort demanded of it, so intense exertion completes the drift from moral debt to sheer physical cost.
senses.whyCN: 身体本身也能为被要求的努力付出代价，于是高强度消耗完成了从道德亏欠到纯粹身体代价的漂移。

intro.en: Punish came into English through Old French punir from Latin punire, an earlier form poenire built on poena 'penalty'. The same poena family also produced penal, penalty and punitive. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punish 经古法语 punir 进入英语，上溯拉丁 punire，其较早形式 poenire 由 poena「罚」构成；同一个 poena 词族还生出 penal、penalty 与 punitive。年代均为约数。

items.en: The Greek noun poine named the price paid to settle a wrong, and it was borrowed into Latin as the starting point of this family.
items.cn: 希腊名词 poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，它被借入拉丁语，成为这一词族的起点。

items.en: Poena meant punishment and also the compensation that settled a wrong, and from it the verb poenire was formed.
items.cn: poena 既指处罚，也指平息过错的补偿，动词 poenire 由它构成。

items.en: Punire replaced the older poenire and meant to inflict a penalty, to avenge, to take vengeance for a wrong.
items.cn: punire 取代了较早的 poenire，意为施加处罚、报复、为过错索取代价。

items.en: Old French punir carried the Latin verb into the sense of correcting by pain, and English borrowed it around 1300.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 把这一拉丁动词带入「以痛苦纠正」的意思，英语大约在十四世纪初借入。

items.en: English punish first meant to inflict a legal penalty, then any painful correction, and finally rough handling of people or things.
items.cn: 英语 punish 最初指施加法律上的处罚，随后泛指任何带来痛苦的纠正，最后扩展到对人、对物的粗暴对待。

items.en: Punishment names the suffering as a result, punishable names what may be punished, and punitive names the intention behind a measure.
items.cn: punishment 把痛苦作为结果来命名，punishable 指可以受罚的，punitive 则指一项措施背后的惩罚意图。

note.en: The first group holds the same Latin family plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of making someone suffer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「使人受苦」这一动作的近义替代。

entries.definition: The noun naming the suffering imposed; the verb names the act of imposing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被施加的痛苦的名词；动词则指施加这一动作。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'liable to be punished'; it describes a legal status, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可受处罚的」形容词；它描述的是一种法律状态，而不是动作。

entries.definition: From Latin punire with an adjective suffix; it describes the purpose of a measure rather than the deed itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 punire 加形容词后缀而来；它描述一项措施的目的，而不是行为本身。

entries.definition: Weak and small; it merely looks like punish at the start and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦小虚弱的；只是开头与 punish 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: To impose a penalty, usually under a written rule; it stresses the rule, while punish stresses the suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 通常依据成文规则施加处罚；它强调规则，而 punish 强调痛苦。

entries.definition: To correct behaviour through training or punishment; reform is the aim, which punish does not imply.
entries.definitionCN: 通过训练或惩罚纠正行为；改正是目的，punish 并不含此意。

entries.definition: To punish or scold severely; it often means words rather than physical suffering and sounds formal.
entries.definitionCN: 严厉惩罚或斥责；常指言语而非肉体痛苦，语体正式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to punishment'; it cannot take an object and never names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与刑罚有关的」形容词；它不能带宾语，也不指动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real derived family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的派生词族与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Punish goes back through French punir to Latin punire, and behind punire stands poena, the price of a wrong.
normal.cn: punish 经法语 punir 上溯拉丁 punire，而 punire 背后站着 poena，即过错的代价。

normal.en: The family keeps splitting the same idea: punishment is the suffering, punitive is the intention, punishable is the liability.
normal.cn: 这一词族不断拆分同一个观念：punishment 是那份痛苦，punitive 是那种意图，punishable 是那种责任。

normal.en: Punish almost always asks two questions: who suffers, and for what.
normal.cn: punish 几乎总要回答两个问题：谁受苦，以及为了什么。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the legal core: punish offenders, punish wrongdoing, be punished by law.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出法律内核：惩罚违法者、惩处不当行为、受法律制裁。

normal.en: The object can be a person, a body, a pair of shoes or an opponent, but the verb always means someone or something pays.
normal.cn: 宾语可以是人、身体、一双鞋或一个对手，但这个动词始终表示「有人或某物在偿付」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the wrong sits on one pan and the suffering is poured onto the other until the beam levels.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一端放着过错，另一端被倒进痛苦，直到横梁齐平。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed to someone who never asked to buy anything.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被递给一个根本没打算买东西的人。

abstract.en: Picture a path of sharp stones laid across a field so that every step costs the walker something.
abstract.cn: 想象田野上铺着一条尖石小路，每走一步都要让行人付出点代价。

examples.en: The school punished the boys for vandalising the gym.
examples.cn: 学校因这些男孩破坏体育馆而惩罚了他们。

examples.en: Years of heavy loads had punished the truck's suspension.
examples.cn: 多年的重载已经把卡车的悬挂系统损耗得很厉害。

examples.en: The home side punished every mistake in the second half.
examples.cn: 主队在下半场抓住了每一次失误并加以重创。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕你失」——怕你失了规矩，就先让你吃一阵苦头 → 惩罚、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「罚、补偿」→ 拉丁动词 poenire / punire「施罚、索偿」→ 古法语 punir → 英语 punish；同族词有 punishment、punishable、punitive、penal、penalty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: a wrong creates a debt, and suffering collects it. The collection can be a general punishment, a court sentence, a parent's correction, deliberate harshness, wear on an object, a heavy defeat, sharp criticism, or plain physical exhaustion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一条线展开：过错生出一笔债，而痛苦负责把它收回。收回的方式可以是泛指的惩罚、法庭的判决、父母的管教、刻意的严酷、对物品的损耗、一场惨败、尖锐的批评，或纯粹的身体消耗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mallet falls and the offender leaves his seat to bear the pain he brought about.
core.cn: 核心意象：木槌落下，犯错的人离开座位，去承受自己招来的那阵疼痛。

branches.en: BASE ACT: pain is deliberately dealt out because a wrong was done.
branches.cn: 基础动作：因为有人做错，痛苦被刻意施加出去。

branches.en: TWO COURTS: the debt is collected by a judge with a sentence, or by a parent with a withdrawn privilege.
branches.cn: 两种法庭：债由法官以判决收取，或由父母以收回特权收取。

branches.en: HARSHNESS WITHOUT A RULE: suffering continues even when no rule existed to be broken.
branches.cn: 无规之严：即便没有可供违反的规则，痛苦仍被继续施加。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN TARGETS: an object wears out under rough use, or an opponent is crushed by a score.
branches.cn: 非人对象：物品在粗暴使用下损耗，对手被比分碾碎。

branches.en: COST WITHOUT A VERDICT: words wound a reputation, and effort wrings out the body.
branches.cn: 无判决的代价：言语损伤名声，用力榨干身体。

intro.en: Punish sits at the head of an English family whose members split the ideas of act, result, liability and purpose.
intro.cn: punish 位于一个英语词族的首位，其成员分别承担动作、结果、责任与目的这几层意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and the verb punire underlie punish, punishment, punishable and punitive, while the adjective poenalis leads to penal and penalty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与动词 punire 位于 punish、punishment、punishable 与 punitive 之下，而形容词 poenalis 则通向 penal 与 penalty。
