definition_zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
definition_en: the reason for which something is done, made or exists
core_image: 木匠在工作台上把一块木板摆正，用粉线弹出一条笔直的线，才落下第一锯
scene: 开工之前，工头把图纸摊在木板上，用手指按住那条基准线，说明这块料为什么要留厚两毫米。The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
sceneCN: 这里 purpose 指「做某件事所依据的目的」（第 1 个义项：意图与目的）；句意为多留那两毫米是为了还能再刨一次。图中可辨识物件：摊开的图纸、按住基准线的手指、弹过粉线的木板、留下的余量；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「有明确目的的」
由名词加副词后缀构成，语义由「意图」转为「故意地」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「没有目的的」
由名词与过去分词复合而成，语义由「用途」转为「专为某用途建造的」
加表示「多」的前缀构成，语义由「用途」转为「一物多用的」

senses.title: The reason for an act
senses.titleCN: 做一件事的理由与意图
senses.definition: the reason one has in mind for doing something or for making something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事或造某物时心里所抱的理由
senses.example: The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
senses.exampleCN: 多留那两毫米，是为了还能再刨一次。
senses.why: the word comes from putting something forward, so a purpose is the aim a person sets in front of the work before starting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自「把某物摆到前面」，因此目的就是开工前把目标摆在工作前面的那件事。

senses.title: The function of a thing
senses.definition: the job that an object or a part is designed to perform
senses.definitionCN: 一件物件或部件被造出来所要承担的功能
senses.example: This room has outlived its original purpose as a laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子原本用作洗衣房，如今那个用途早已过去了。
senses.why: the aim moves from the maker's head into the made thing, where it becomes a function.
senses.whyCN: 目标从造物者的脑子里移到被造之物里，在那里它就成了一种功能。

senses.title: Firmness of intention
senses.definition: resolute determination to carry out what one has decided
senses.definitionCN: 把已经决定的事做到底的那份坚决
senses.example: He spoke with purpose and nobody interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话带着决心，没人打断。
senses.why: a settled intention shows in the manner of speech, and the noun then names the firmness rather than the aim.
senses.whyCN: 已定的意图会显现在说话的方式上，此时名词指的是那份坚定，而不是目标。

senses.title: Relevance to the matter
senses.definition: the quality of bearing on the question at hand, as in remarks that are to the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与眼前问题相干的品质，如「切题」的话
senses.example: Every question was to the purpose, and the meeting ended early.
senses.exampleCN: 每个问题都切中正题，会议提前结束。
senses.why: what is aimed at the matter in hand is relevant, so a fixed phrase marks this older, narrower sense.
senses.whyCN: 对准眼前事务的就是相关的，因此一个固定说法保存了这条更窄的旧义。

senses.title: Meaning in a life
senses.definition: the sense that one's existence or work has a point worth serving
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己的存在或工作有一个值得效力的要点
senses.example: Teaching gave her a purpose she had not found in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 教书给了她一种在实验室里没找到的意义。
senses.why: when the aim is large enough to organize a life, the word shifts from a task to a reason for living.
senses.whyCN: 当目标大到足以组织一生，这个词就从一项任务转为活着的理由。

senses.title: A stated aim of an institution
senses.definition: the declared aim that a body, a fund or a law is set up to serve
senses.definitionCN: 一个机构、基金或法律被设立时所声明的目标
senses.example: The fund's purpose is written on its first page.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金的宗旨写在第一页上。
senses.why: organizations must put their aim forward in writing, which keeps the original image of placing something in front.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须把目标写在前面，这保留了「把某物摆到前面」的原初意象。

senses.title: Result actually achieved
senses.definition: the outcome that an action actually produces, as in efforts that came to good purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一个行动实际产生的效果，如「见了效」的努力
senses.example: All the digging came to good purpose when the well struck water.
senses.exampleCN: 井里出水时，所有挖掘都见了效。
senses.why: an aim that is realized becomes a result, and older English used the noun for that realized effect.
senses.whyCN: 实现的目标会变成结果，旧时英语就用这个名词指那种已实现的效用。

senses.title: A proposal or intent
senses.definition: a plan or proposal one puts forward, the sense closest to the French source
senses.definitionCN: 一个人摆出来的计划或提议，是最贴近法语来源的一层
senses.example: Their purpose was to rebuild the mill before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的打算是在入冬前把磨坊重建起来。
senses.why: the French ancestor meant a proposal put forward, and this plain sense still surfaces in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语祖词意为「摆出来的提议」，这一朴素义仍会在正式文字中浮现。

intro.en: Purpose comes through Old French porpos 'aim, intention' from porposer 'to put forth', a variant of proposer, which rests on Latin proponere 'to put forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ponere 'to place'. The deeper origin of ponere is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 porpos「目标、意图」来自 porposer「摆出、提出」，那是 proposer 的变体，其源头是拉丁 proponere「放到前面」，由 pro-「向前」与 ponere「放置」构成。ponere 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the proposal that links it to a root for 'to place' is circular and adds nothing, so the source is best left open.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。其更深来源不确定；把它与另一个同样表示「放置」的词根相联系只是循环解释，并无增益，因此来源宜存疑。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ponere gave proponere 'to put forward, set before one', used of plans, terms and proposals.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ponere 构成 proponere「摆到前面、置于眼前」，用于计划、条款与提议。

items.en: Old French porposer 'to put forth, intend' produced the noun porpos, which named both the aim and the resolve behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 porposer「提出、打算」产生名词 porpos，兼指目标与背后的决心。

items.en: Middle English took purpose for an intention, and the phrase on purpose later fixed the sense of doing something deliberately.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词表示意图，后来固定说法「故意地」把「有意为之」的意思定了下来。

items.en: Modern law and administration use the noun for the declared aim of a body, which is the oldest image of putting an aim in front of the work.
items.cn: 现代法律与行政用这个名词指机构声明的宗旨，这正是「把目标摆在工作前面」最古老的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ponere and the exact date of the deliberateness phrase): no citation fixes the first use for an institution's aim, and any Indo-European form offered for ponere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ponere 的更深来源与「故意」说法确切成形的年代）：机构宗旨义没有确切的最早书证；凡为 ponere 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates verbs and nouns built on the same placing root; group two separates words for an aim by how explicit it is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「放置」词根的动词与名词；第二组按明确程度区分表示「目标」的词。

entries.definition: The direct relative: to put a plan or an offer before others, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 最直接的同族词：把计划或提议摆到别人面前，同出那个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From the same placing verb through French: to put something forward, hence to set a question or hold a position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「放置」动词经法语而来：把某物摆出，因而指提出问题或摆出姿势。

entries.definition: In- 'upon' plus ponere: to place a burden on someone, which is the same root pressing downward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「在上」加 ponere 构成：把负担压在别人身上，同一词根往下用力。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: to put parts together, hence to write or to calm oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 ponere 构成：把部件放到一起，因而指写作或使镇定。

entries.definition: From pro- plus portare 'to carry': to carry a meaning or a claim, with no placing involved and no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pro- 加 portare「搬运」构成：承载某种含义或声称，不含「放置」，也不同根。

entries.definition: The thing one intends to hit or reach; it is sharper and more specific than purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 打算击中或抵达的东西；比 purpose 更尖锐、更具体。

entries.definition: A defined end point one can mark and check; purpose is broader and can be a reason rather than a finish line.
entries.definitionCN: 一个可标示、可核对的明确终点；purpose 更宽，可以是理由而非终点线。

entries.definition: What a person means to do, often before acting; it is closer to the mental state than to the thing served.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算做什么，多在行动之前；更接近心理状态，而不是所服务的事。

entries.definition: The explanation of why something is as it is; it can look backward, while purpose looks forward.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某事为何如此的理由；可以向后看，而 purpose 向前看。

entries.definition: The work a thing performs; it is the mechanical face of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所执行的工作；是 purpose 在机械层面的面孔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means to place, and the prefix means forward: a purpose is an aim placed in front of the work.
normal.cn: 词根意为「放置」，前缀意为「向前」：目的就是被摆在工作前面的那个目标。

normal.en: The family runs purpose, purposeful, purposely, purposeless, purpose-built, multipurpose.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、形容词、副词、否定式与两个复合词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: on purpose, serve a purpose, fit for purpose, a sense of purpose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：故意地、起作用、适合用途、目标感。

normal.en: The siblings propose, pose, impose and compose all come from the same placing verb.
normal.cn: 同族的 propose、pose、impose 与 compose 都出自那个「放置」动词。

normal.en: The look-alike purport comes from a verb meaning to carry, so it means to claim rather than to intend.
normal.cn: 形近的 purport 出自一个意为「搬运」的动词，所以它的意思是「声称」而非「打算」。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line snapped on a board before the first cut.
abstract.cn: 想象第一锯之前，木板上先弹出的一条粉线。

abstract.en: Picture a sign at the head of a path saying what the path is for.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小路的起点立着一块牌子，写着这条路是为什么修的。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp aimed at one desk rather than lighting the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照一张桌子，而不是照亮整间屋子。

examples.en: The purpose of the new rule is to slow the traffic at the gate.
examples.cn: 新规定的目的是让门口的车辆慢下来。

examples.en: He knocked the cup over on purpose and then apologized.
examples.cn: 他故意碰倒杯子，然后又道了歉。

examples.en: The building has served its purpose and will be pulled down.
examples.cn: 这座楼已经完成它的用途，将被拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「purpose 破的」——先想清楚为什么做，才不容易把事情做破 → 目的

root: 古法语 porpos「目标、意图」← porposer「提出」← 拉丁 proponere「放到前面」= pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）；ponere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: an aim is placed in front of the work, and that placed aim then becomes a function, a firmness, a relevance, a reason for living, an institutional charter, a realized effect and finally a plain proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先把目标摆到工作前面，这个被摆出的目标随后变成一项功能、一份坚定、一种相关性、一个活着的理由、一纸机构宗旨、一个已实现的效果，最后成为一句朴素的提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snapped chalk line laid on a board before the saw goes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：锯子落下之前，先在被板上弹出一条粉线。

branches.en: THE AIM PUT FORWARD: an intention in the mind and a proposal spoken aloud.
branches.cn: 摆出的目标：心里的意图与说出口的提议。

branches.en: THE AIM BUILT IN: one aim settles into a thing's function, another into a body's charter.
branches.cn: 被造进去的目标：一个目标落成物的功能，另一个落成机构的宗旨。

branches.en: THE AIM HELD TIGHT: resolve is the same aim felt as will.
branches.cn: 被握紧的目标：决心就是同一个目标在意志层面的感受。

branches.en: AIMED AND REALIZED: what bears on the matter, and what actually comes of it.
branches.cn: 对准与实现：切中事务的，以及确实做出来的效果。

branches.en: AIM LARGE ENOUGH FOR A LIFE: the aim becomes a reason to get up.
branches.cn: 大到足够撑起一生的目标：目标变成起床的理由。

intro.en: Purpose is a French-shaped noun whose Latin prefix and verb are still productive in English, so its parts can be read clearly.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态的名词，其拉丁前缀与动词在英语里仍有构成力，因此部件读得很清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' gives propose, impose, compose, position and deposit; pro- 'forward' appears in proceed, promote and protect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere「放置」衍生出 propose、impose、compose、position 与 deposit；pro-「向前」见于 proceed、promote 与 protect。

items.example: She purposely left the door open.

items.example: A multipurpose hall serves the whole village.

definition_en: a small bag used for carrying money, especially a woman's handbag; also the money a person or group has available, or the prize money offered in a competition
core_image: 围裙内袋里一只磨旧的皮钱袋，装着一整天的收入
scene: 早市快收摊时，卖菜的女人把零钱一张张理平，塞进围裙内侧的布袋。She kept the day's takings in a worn leather purse.
sceneCN: 这里 purse 是「钱包、随身钱袋」（第 1 个义项：装钱的小包）；句意为她把一天的收入放进一只磨旧的皮钱包里。画面里可留意：围裙、理平的零钱、旧皮袋。

pos.zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金

derivatives.zh: purse 加表人后缀 -er，原指管钱袋的人，现指船上掌管账目与薪水的职务
cut 与 purse 复合，字面是「割钱袋的人」，指旧时的扒手
purse 与 proud 复合，指因富有而傲慢的

senses.title: A small bag for carrying money
senses.definition: a small bag, often with a clasp, used especially by women for carrying money and a few personal items
senses.definitionCN: 尤指女性使用、常带扣合的小包，用来装钱和少量随身物品
senses.example: She took a coin from her purse and paid the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 她从钱包里取出一枚硬币付给司机。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it named a leather bag, and the first English purses were soft pouches pulled shut with strings, long before notes and cards existed.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁词本指皮袋，英语最早的 purse 就是用细绳收口的小软袋，那时还没有纸币和银行卡。

senses.title: The money a person or group can spend
senses.definition: the amount of money that a person, family or organization has available to spend
senses.definitionCN: 个人、家庭或机构手头可供支配的钱
senses.example: The repair cost more than the family purse could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔修缮费超出了这个家庭的财力。
senses.why: Once a container holds money, the container can stand for the contents, and then for the spending power those contents give.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦装着钱，就能代指里面的钱，再进一步指这些钱带来的购买力。

senses.title: Prize money in a competition
senses.definition: the sum of money offered as a prize in a race, a fight or another contest
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑、拳赛或其他比赛中作为奖品的钱
senses.example: The boxer gave his purse to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这名拳手把奖金捐给了村里的学校。
senses.why: Prize money was once handed over in an actual bag at the end of a contest, so the name of the container stayed on the prize after payments moved to cheques.
senses.whyCN: 比赛结束时奖金真的装在一只袋子里当场交付，所以即使后来改用支票，容器之名仍留在奖金上。

intro.en: Purse travels back through Old French and medieval Latin to Latin bursa, a leather bag; the Greek word behind bursa is generally thought to be a borrowing, so anything deeper is uncertain.
intro.cn: purse 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语 bursa（皮袋）；bursa 背后的希腊词一般认为也是借词，再往前的来源并不确定。

items.en: Greek byrsa meant a hide or a leather bag, and it is generally considered a loanword into Greek rather than an inherited item.
items.cn: 希腊语 byrsa 指兽皮或皮袋，一般认为它是借入希腊语的词，而非本土传承。

items.en: Latin bursa named a leather pouch and later a treasury or money chest, which is why the family also touches public money.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 指皮制小袋，后来也指金库、钱柜，所以这个词族也涉及公共资金。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept bursa for a bag and a treasury, while Old French developed borse, the form that carried the word towards England.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留 bursa 指袋子和金库，古法语则发展出 borse，正是把这个词带向英格兰的形式。

items.en: Middle English purs named a small drawstring pouch worn at the belt, carried by men as well as women.
items.cn: 中古英语 purs 指系在腰带上、用细绳收口的小袋，男女都常佩带。

items.en: Everyday modern English narrows the object to a woman's handbag, while the older sense of available money survives in public purse and purse strings.
items.cn: 现代英语日常用法把这个物件收窄为女式手袋，而「可用之钱」的旧义仍活在 public purse 与 purse strings 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same bag word; the near-meaning group collects other words for what holds money or for money itself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「袋」词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收其他表示装钱的物件或钱本身的词。

entries.definition: To follow someone in order to catch them; only the opening letters are similar.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶、追求；只是开头几个字母相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The officer on a ship who keeps the accounts and pays the crew.
entries.definitionCN: 船上负责账目与发放薪水的职务。

entries.definition: An official who manages money in a college or school.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学或学校里管理钱财的职务。

entries.definition: To pay money back to someone who has spent it on your behalf.
entries.definitionCN: 把别人替你垫付的钱还给他。

entries.definition: A small flat case for notes and cards, usually carried in a pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 装纸币与卡片的小扁夹，通常放在口袋里。

entries.definition: A bag for personal items, carried especially by women.
entries.definitionCN: 装随身物品的包，尤指女性提包。

entries.definition: Money set aside for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个用途准备的钱。

entries.definition: A shared sum of money collected from a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人凑起来共用的一笔钱。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to a leather bag, and every later sense still keeps something of that one small container.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自一只皮袋，后来每个义项都还留着那只小容器的影子。

normal.en: Bursa in Latin is a leather pouch, and the earliest English purses were exactly that: soft bags closed with string.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 是皮制小袋，英语最早的 purse 正是这种用细绳收口的软袋。

normal.en: Purser keeps the money-handling side of the family: the person on a ship who looks after accounts and pay.
normal.cn: purser 保留了词族中「管钱」的一面：船上负责账目与薪水的人。

normal.en: Reimburse puts re- (back) with a stem from bursa, so the word pictures money going back into the bag it came from.
normal.cn: reimburse 把表示「回」的 re- 与 bursa 的词干结合，画面就是钱回到原来的袋子里。

normal.en: Purse strings were once literal cords; holding them now means controlling the money itself.
normal.cn: purse strings 从前是实实在在的绳子，如今握住它就等于掌控钱财。

normal.en: The public purse treats a whole country's funds as one bag that officials must open with care.
normal.cn: public purse 把一个国家的资金看成一只袋子，官员打开它时必须谨慎。

abstract.en: A purse fits in one hand, yet it can stand for everything a household is able to choose.
abstract.cn: 钱袋一只手就握得住，却可以代表一个家庭所能做的一切选择。

abstract.en: One word names the bag, the money and the prize, because each is something handed from one person to another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指袋子、又指钱和奖金，因为这三样都是从一个人手里交到另一个人手里。

abstract.en: A purse is often closed not by its clasp but by the fear behind it.
abstract.cn: 钱袋往往是靠背后的顾虑合上的，而不是靠那道扣子。

examples.en: She paid the fare from a small purse she kept in her coat.
examples.cn: 她用外套里一只小钱包付了车费。

examples.en: The tour was cancelled because the club's purse was empty.
examples.cn: 巡演取消了，因为俱乐部的资金已经见底。

examples.en: The winner took home a purse of fifty thousand dollars.
examples.cn: 冠军拿走了五万美元奖金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「珀斯」——去澳大利亚的珀斯旅行，得先备好钱包，记住 purse 是钱包、财力。

root: 拉丁语 bursa（皮袋、钱袋）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入中古英语作 purs；同族词多与袋、钱、偿付有关，如 purser、reimburse。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bag that holds money; the senses divide into the bag itself, the money inside it, and the prize once handed over in such a bag.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是装钱的袋子；义项由此分为袋子本身、袋里的钱，以及从前装在这种袋子里交付的奖金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn leather pouch tucked inside an apron, holding a whole day's earnings.
core.cn: 核心意象：围裙内侧一只磨旧的皮袋，装着一整天的收入。

branches.en: a drawstring pouch on a market stall
branches.cn: 集市摊前一只收口的钱袋

branches.en: a bag whose weight equals a family's choices
branches.cn: 一只袋子的分量等于一个家庭的选择

branches.en: a council counting what it can afford
branches.cn: 市政会算着手里的钱够做什么

branches.en: a prize handed over in a leather bag
branches.cn: 装在皮袋里当场交付的奖金

branches.en: money that is both kept and awarded
branches.cn: 既被存着又被颁出去的同一笔钱

intro.en: The word is held together by a Greek bag word, its Latin descendant, the English noun, and the suffixes that build a person and a paying-back verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「袋」、它的拉丁后裔、英语名词，以及构成「人」与「偿付」的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a leather pouch, later a treasury
an officer who handles money on a ship
the cords once used to close a bag

latinEntries.meaning: one who keeps a purse or treasury

definition_zh: 推；推动；催促；推销；攻势
definition_en: to press something so that it moves away from you; to urge someone to act; to promote a product or idea; also a strong coordinated effort to achieve something
core_image: 两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽
scene: 货车在坡道上熄了火，司机跳下来，绕到车尾，双手抵住厢板。He pushed hard until the wheels began to turn.
sceneCN: 这里 push 是「用力推」（第 1 个义项：施加力量使物体移动）；句意为他一直用力推，直到车轮开始转动。画面里可留意：货车、坡道、车尾厢板。

derivatives.zh: push 加表人后缀 -er，指推的人，口语中也指贩毒者
push 加 -y 构成形容词，指过分急于达到目的、咄咄逼人的
push 与 up 复合，指靠双臂把身体撑起的俯卧撑
push 与 back 复合，指推回去的力量，现多指反对与抵制

senses.title: To press something away from you
senses.definition: to press a person or thing so that it moves away from you or moves forward
senses.definitionCN: 按住人或物，使它离开你或向前移动
senses.example: He pushed the door open with one shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一边肩膀把门顶开了。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word meant to beat or drive, so the earliest English sense is a hand or a body driving an object forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁动词本义是击打、驱赶，所以英语最早的义项就是用手或身体把东西向前顶开。

senses.title: To urge someone to act
senses.definition: to urge or pressure someone to do something, especially when they are slow or unwilling
senses.definitionCN: 催促或施压让某人去做某事，尤指对方迟缓或不情愿时
senses.example: The teacher pushed the class to finish before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 老师催全班在中午前做完。
senses.why: A hand can move a thing, and the same force can be applied to a person's will, so physical pressure becomes social pressure.
senses.whyCN: 手能推动物体，同样的力气也能加到人的意愿上，于是身体的推变成了人际的催逼。

senses.title: To promote a product or idea
senses.definition: to try hard to sell a product or to make an idea accepted by many people
senses.definitionCN: 努力卖出产品，或让某个想法被许多人接受
senses.example: The company pushed its new phone through every channel it had.
senses.exampleCN: 公司用尽所有渠道推销它的新手机。
senses.why: Selling is moving goods towards buyers, so the verb for moving an object forward was borrowed for moving goods out of the shop.
senses.whyCN: 销售就是把货物推向买家，于是「把东西往前推」的动词被借来指把货推出店门。

senses.title: A determined campaign or advance
senses.definition: a planned and forceful effort to achieve something, or a military advance
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某事而组织起来的一次有力行动，或军事上的推进
senses.example: The union began a push for shorter hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会开始了一场争取缩短工时的行动。
senses.why: Beside the verb grew a noun: the whole forward movement, repeated by many hands, became a single campaign with a name.
senses.whyCN: 动词旁边长出了名词：许多人一次次向前使力，整体就成了有名字的一场行动。

intro.en: Push came from Old French pousser, whose Latin ancestor pulsare meant to beat or strike repeatedly; the same Latin family also gave English pulse and compel.
intro.cn: push 来自古法语 pousser，其拉丁语祖先是 pulsare（反复击打）；同一拉丁词族还给英语带来了 pulse 与 compel。

items.en: Pellere meant to drive, strike or set in motion, and it stands behind a large family of Latin verbs of movement.
items.cn: pellere 意为驱动、击打、使动，是拉丁语一大批运动动词的共同源头。

items.en: Pulsare was a frequentative of pellere, meaning to beat or knock again and again, as a hand does on a door.
items.cn: pulsare 是 pellere 的反复动词，意为一下一下地击打，像手在门上敲个不停。

items.en: Old French pousser meant to push or thrust and is the form English borrowed; the older spelling poulser is also recorded.
items.cn: 古法语 pousser 意为推、顶，英语借的正是这个形式；文献中还有更早的拼写 poulser。

items.en: English attests pushen in the thirteenth century, at first for bodily shoving and soon for pressing an argument or a claim.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪已见 pushen，起初指身体上的推搡，很快也用于推进某个论点或主张。

items.en: Modern English extends the verb to advertising, queues, prices and campaigns, while the noun keeps the sense of one coordinated forward movement.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到广告、排队、价格与竞选，名词则保留「一次协同的向前推进」之意。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin root of beating and driving; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「击打、驱动」词根上的词；近义组收其他表示用力移动某物的动词。

entries.definition: To beat or throb with a regular rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律地跳动、搏动。

entries.definition: A single beat of the heart or of a regular wave.
entries.definitionCN: 心脏或规律波动的一次搏动。

entries.definition: To force someone to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使某人做某事。

entries.definition: To drive something back or keep it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物击退或挡开。

entries.definition: To push someone or something roughly.
entries.definitionCN: 粗暴地推人或推物。

entries.definition: To push gently, often with the elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻一推，常指用手肘碰。

entries.definition: To drive something forward with sudden force.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地向前推送。

entries.definition: To push steadily against something.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地压、按。

normalIntro.en: The word descends from a Latin verb of beating, and its senses all keep the picture of force applied at one point.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语中表示击打的动词，各个义项都保留着「在一点上使力」的画面。

normal.en: Pellere drives and pulsare beats; push is the repeated beat that finally moves the object.
normal.cn: pellere 是驱动，pulsare 是反复击打；push 就是那一下下敲击终于把东西推动了。

normal.en: Old French pousser is the direct source, which is why push looks nothing like its Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: 古法语 pousser 是直接来源，所以 push 的拼写与它的拉丁祖先毫无相似之处。

normal.en: Pushy adds -y to the action and turns it into a personality that keeps pressing other people.
normal.cn: pushy 在动作后加 -y，把「推」变成一种不断对别人施压的性格。

normal.en: A push-up is the body lifting itself by pushing down on the floor.
normal.cn: push-up 是靠向下推地面把身体撑起来的动作。

normal.en: Pushback is the force that returns when you push, now used mostly for people resisting a plan.
normal.cn: pushback 是你推出去之后返回来的一股力，如今多指人们对某项计划的抵制。

abstract.en: Force applied at one point can move a whole object, which is why the word suits hands, campaigns and markets alike.
abstract.cn: 作用在一点上的力能移动整个物体，所以这个词既能用于手，也能用于运动和推广。

abstract.en: A society moves forward when someone grows tired enough of standing still to start pushing.
abstract.cn: 社会往前动，往往是因为有人厌倦了原地不动，开始使力。

abstract.en: Pushing and pulling are the two directions of every bargain, and most deals settle somewhere between them.
abstract.cn: 推与拉是每场讨价还价的两种方向，多数交易最终落在两者之间。

examples.en: She pushed the heavy box across the floor.
examples.cn: 她把那只沉重的箱子推过地板。

examples.en: The campaign pushed hard for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 这场运动为争取更清洁的空气大力施压。

examples.en: One final push got the team over the line.
examples.cn: 最后一次发力让队伍越过了终点线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「布什」——布什总统一挥手，把前面的人往前一推，记住 push 是推。

root: 古法语 pousser（推）← 拉丁语 pulsare（反复击打）← pellere（驱动、击打）；同族有 pulse、compel、repel。

sensesIntro.en: The core is force applied at a point; the senses divide into moving an object, pressing a person, selling goods, and one organized forward effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是在一点上使力；义项由此分为推动物体、催逼他人、推销货物，以及一次有组织的推进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms flat against a heavy door, the gap widening by a finger's width.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手掌抵住一扇沉门，门缝一点点变宽。

branches.en: a palm flat against a stuck door
branches.cn: 一只手掌平贴在卡住的门上

branches.en: a hand on someone's back at the start line
branches.cn: 起跑线上按在他人后背的手

branches.en: a new phone in every window display
branches.cn: 每个橱窗里都摆着的新手机

branches.en: a march moving one field closer
branches.cn: 向前推进一地的行军

branches.en: pressure that moves a person and a whole group
branches.cn: 推动一个人也推动一群人的力量

intro.en: The word is held together by two Latin verbs of driving and beating, an Old French verb, and English suffixes that make a person and a quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个表示驱动与击打的拉丁动词、一个古法语动词，以及构成「人」与「性质」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: too eager to get what one wants
items.meaningCN: 过分急于得到；咄咄逼人的

definition_zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于某种状态；推迟
definition_en: to move something into a position and leave it there; to express something in words; to cause someone or something to be in a state; in put off, to delay
core_image: 一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开
scene: 夜深了，母亲把洗好的碗一只只擦干，转身走向橱柜。She put the plates on the top shelf and closed the door.
sceneCN: 这里 put 是「放置」（第 1 个义项：把东西放到某处）；句意为她把盘子放到最上层架子上，然后关上柜门。画面里可留意：擦干的碗、橱柜、最上层架子。

pos.zh: 放；放置；表达；使处于；推迟

derivatives.zh: in 与 put 复合，指放进系统的内容，即输入
out 与 put 复合，指系统送出的结果，即产出
put 与 down 复合，指把人压低的话，即贬损
put 与 on 复合，指装出来的样子，即做作

senses.title: To place something somewhere
senses.definition: to move something into a position and leave it there
senses.definitionCN: 把某物移到某个位置并留在那里
senses.example: She put the keys beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她把钥匙放在门边。
senses.why: The earliest recorded sense is simply to set a thing down and let go, and almost every other sense grows out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早义项就是把东西放下然后松手，其余义项几乎都从这幅画面长出来。

senses.title: To express something in words
senses.definition: to say or write something in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式说出或写出某事
senses.example: How should I put this so nobody is hurt?
senses.exampleCN: 这话我该怎么说才不伤人？
senses.why: Words are placed into a sentence the way objects are placed on a table, so arranging language took the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 词被安放进句子，就像东西被摆到桌面上，于是「安排语言」也用了同一个动词。

senses.title: To cause someone to be in a state
senses.definition: to cause someone or something to be in a particular situation or condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物进入某种处境或状态
senses.example: The new rule put everyone under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让每个人都感到了压力。
senses.why: If a thing can be placed in a spot, a person can be placed in a condition, and the verb then means to bring that condition about.
senses.whyCN: 东西既能被放到某个位置，人也能被放进某种处境，于是这个动词就表示「使某种处境发生」。

senses.title: To delay something, in put off
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb put off, to move an event or an action to a later time
senses.definitionCN: 在短语动词 put off 中，把一件事或一个行动挪到以后
senses.example: They put off the meeting until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议推迟到周五。
senses.why: Putting a thing off is putting it away from the present moment, so the spatial verb turns into a verb about time.
senses.whyCN: 把一件事推开，就是把它从当下这一刻挪走，于是空间上的动词转成了时间上的动词。

intro.en: The origin of put is uncertain. It is first recorded in Middle English, and it may come from Old English, from Old Norse pota, or from Old French bouter, all of which suggest a gesture of thrusting or placing; no reliable Latin cognate exists.
intro.cn: put 的来源不确定。它最早见于中古英语，可能来自古英语，也可能来自古诺斯语 pota 或古法语 bouter，这些说法都与「推、放」的手势有关；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Old Norse pota meant to poke or thrust, and it is one of the forms often suggested as a source; the link is possible rather than proved.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 pota 意为戳、推，是常被提出的来源之一；这只是可能，并未得到确证。

items.en: Some scholars reconstruct an Old English verb putian, but it is not attested in surviving texts, so it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 有学者为古英语重构出动词 putian，但现存文献中并无此词，所以它仍只是假说。

items.en: Old French bouter meant to thrust or shove and may have reinforced the English word, especially in southern dialects.
items.cn: 古法语 bouter 意为推、顶，可能在英格兰南部方言中加强了这个英语词。

items.en: Middle English putten is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of placing something somewhere.
items.cn: 中古英语 putten 自十四世纪起有记录，意为把某物放到某处。

items.en: Modern English keeps the irregular past put and builds a wide range of phrasal verbs such as put off, put up with and put forward.
items.cn: 现代英语保留不规则的过去式 put，并构成 put off、put up with、put forward 等大量短语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built with put and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group collects other verbs of placing.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 构成的复合词以及几个只是外形相近的词；近义组收其他表示放置的动词。

entries.definition: Data, energy or effort fed into a system.
entries.definitionCN: 输入系统的数据、能量或投入。

entries.definition: What a system produces after processing its input.
entries.definitionCN: 系统处理输入之后产生的结果。

entries.definition: A gentle stroke in golf; the word comes from Scottish and is not the verb of placing.
entries.definitionCN: 高尔夫中的轻推击球；这个词来自苏格兰语，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A soft paste used to fix glass into a frame; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 把玻璃固定到框子里的软膏；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To fix something in a particular position or spot.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物安放到特定位置。

entries.definition: To place an object carefully in a chosen spot.
entries.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放在选定的地方。

entries.definition: To spread something flat on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物平放在表面上。

entries.definition: To arrange something deliberately for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的有意摆放某物。

normalIntro.en: The word has one unchanging past form, and its many phrasal verbs all move things in space or in time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的过去式只有一种写法，而它的大量短语动词都在空间或时间里挪动东西。

normal.en: Put keeps the same form for the past, so only the rest of the sentence tells you when it happened.
normal.cn: put 的过去式与原型同形，只能靠句子的其余部分判断时间。

normal.en: Input and output are put with in and out: what is put in and what is put out.
normal.cn: input 与 output 就是 put 加 in 与 out：放进去的东西与送出来的东西。

normal.en: A put-down is a remark that places a person lower than they stood a moment before.
normal.cn: put-down 是一句话，把一个人放到比片刻之前更低的位置。

normal.en: Put off moves an event away from now, while put up with means to hold up under something.
normal.cn: put off 把一件事挪离当下，put up with 则是把某件事忍下来。

normal.en: Learners often master this verb last because every regular ending would sound wrong to a native ear.
normal.cn: 学习者往往最后才掌握这个动词，因为任何规则变化的词尾在本族语者听来都不对。

abstract.en: To put is to decide where a thing belongs, if only for the next minute.
abstract.cn: 放，就是决定一样东西该在哪儿，哪怕只为下一分钟。

abstract.en: Every sentence is a row of things put in order, which is why one verb serves both the table and the tongue.
abstract.cn: 每个句子都是把东西排好的一行，所以同一个动词既管桌面也管舌头。

abstract.en: Putting something off is storing it in the future, and the future is where unfinished things collect.
abstract.cn: 把事情推迟，就是把它存进未来，而未完成的事总在未来堆积。

examples.en: Please put the chairs back where you found them.
examples.cn: 请把椅子放回你原来找到的地方。

examples.en: She put her objection in the mildest words she could find.
examples.cn: 她用能找到的最温和的说法表达了反对。

examples.en: The match was put off because of the storm.
examples.cn: 比赛因暴风雨推迟了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「葡挞」——一盒葡挞往桌上一放，就记住 put 是放。

root: 中古英语 putten，可能与古诺斯语 pota（戳、推）或古法语 bouter（推）有关；没有可靠的拉丁同族词，来源一般标为不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand setting an object down; the senses divide into placing, wording, causing a state, and moving something into the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一只手把物体放下；义项由此分为放置、措辞、使进入某种状态，以及把某事挪到以后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand setting a cup firmly on a table, then letting go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把杯子稳稳放到桌面上，随即松开。

branches.en: a cup set down and released
branches.cn: 放下并松开手的杯子

branches.en: a sentence built like a shelf
branches.cn: 像架子一样搭起来的句子

branches.en: a person standing inside a new rule
branches.cn: 站在新规定里的人

branches.en: a meeting moved to another page of the calendar
branches.cn: 被挪到日历另一页的会议

branches.en: the same hand moving things in space and in time
branches.cn: 同一只手在空间与时间里挪动东西

intro.en: The word is held together by a Germanic verb of uncertain origin, a Middle English form, and English compounds that place something in or out.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个来源不确定的日耳曼语动词、一个中古英语形式，以及表示「放入、送出」的英语复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the forms behind it are Germanic and Romance, and its origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词；它背后的形式分属日耳曼语与罗曼语，来源并不确定。

items.meaning: to place, to express, to delay
what is fed into a system
to delay to a later time

definition_zh: 四分之一；一刻钟；季度；城区；一节；住所
definition_en: one of four equal parts; fifteen minutes; a period of three months; a district of a city; one of the periods of a game; a place where someone lives
core_image: 一块圆饼被刀切成四等份，其中一份被叉子轻轻挑起
scene: 球场的计时牌跳进最后一格，观众站起来看表，教练把手里的战术板攥紧。The home team scored twice in the final quarter of the game.
sceneCN: 这里 quarter 是「比赛的一节」（第 5 个义项：一场比赛被分成的四段之一）；句意为主队在比赛的最后一节两次得分。画面里可留意：计时牌、战术板、站起来的观众。

pos.zh: 四分之一；一刻钟；季度；城区；一节；住所

derivatives.zh: quarter 加 -ly，指每季度一次的，也可作副词与名词
quarter 与 final 复合，指四分之一决赛，即八进四的那一轮
head 与 quarters 复合，指总部所在之处，字面是「首要的营房」

senses.title: One of four equal parts
senses.definition: one of four equal parts into which a whole is divided
senses.definitionCN: 一个整体被分成四份时的其中一份
senses.example: A quarter of the class chose to walk to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 班里四分之一的人选择走路去博物馆。
senses.why: Latin quartarius named a fourth part, and English kept the plain fraction sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quartarius 指第四份，英语把这个最朴素的分数义保留在词的核心。

senses.title: Fifteen minutes
senses.definition: one fourth of an hour, used especially in telling the time
senses.definitionCN: 一小时的四分之一，尤用于报时
senses.example: The train leaves at a quarter past six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车六点一刻出发。
senses.why: Since an hour divides neatly into four, the fourth part of an hour became the everyday name for fifteen minutes.
senses.whyCN: 既然一小时正好能分成四份，一小时的四分之一就成了十五分钟的日常说法。

senses.title: A period of three months
senses.definition: one of the four three-month periods into which a business or school year is divided
senses.definitionCN: 商业或学年被分成的四个三个月周期之一
senses.example: Sales rose sharply in the last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 销售额在最后一个季度大幅上升。
senses.why: A year is four quarters, so the fourth part of a year became the standard unit of business reporting.
senses.whyCN: 一年有四个季度，于是「一年的四分之一」成了商业报表的标准单位。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.definition: an area of a city, especially one with its own character
senses.definitionCN: 城市中一片区域，尤指有自身特色的区域
senses.example: The old quarter is full of narrow lanes and small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区满是狭窄的巷子和小店铺。
senses.why: Old French quartier meant a fourth part of a town as well as a lodging, and the place sense survived in English.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 quartier 既指城镇的四分之一区，也指住处，这层「地方」的意思在英语里保留了下来。

senses.title: One of the periods of a game
senses.titleCN: 一节；一局中的四分之一
senses.definition: one of the four periods into which some sports divide their playing time
senses.definitionCN: 某些运动把比赛时间分成的四段之一
senses.example: He scored twice in the final quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一节两次得分。
senses.why: Sports that divide play into four equal periods simply call each period a quarter.
senses.whyCN: 把比赛分成四个等长时段的运动项目，就直接把每一段叫作 quarter。

senses.title: A place to live
senses.definition: a place where soldiers or staff live, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 士兵或员工的住处，通常用复数
senses.example: The crew returned to their quarters after the drill.
senses.exampleCN: 演习结束后，船员们回到自己的住处。
senses.why: To quarter troops meant to lodge them in a district, and the plural quarters came to mean the lodgings themselves.
senses.whyCN: to quarter troops 本指把军队安排到某片区域驻扎，复数 quarters 由此转指住处本身。

intro.en: Quarter comes from the Latin word for a fourth part, formed from the ordinal fourth and carried into English through French.
intro.cn: quarter 源自拉丁语表示「第四份」的词，由序数词「第四」构成，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quartus was the ordinal fourth, the root of a whole family of words about dividing something into four.
items.cn: quartus 是序数词「第四」，是一整族关于把事物四等分的词的根。

items.en: Quartarius named a fourth part, whether of a measure, of a day or of a town.
items.cn: quartarius 指第四份，无论是度量、一天还是一座城镇的第四份。

items.en: Old French quartier meant both a fourth part and a district or lodging place.
items.cn: 古法语 quartier 既指第四份，也指一片城区或住处。

items.en: Middle English quarter took the fraction sense and added the senses of time and place.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quarter 接受了分数义，又增加了时间与地点两层意思。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for fractions, for fifteen minutes, for business periods, for city areas and for sports periods.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指分数、十五分钟、商业周期、城区与比赛时段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of fourth; the near-meaning group gathers words for fractions, districts and set periods.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「第四」词干上的词；近义组收表示分数、城区与固定时段的词。

entries.definition: A unit of liquid measure equal to two pints.
entries.definitionCN: 等于两品脱的液量单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every three months.
entries.definitionCN: 每三个月发生一次的。

entries.definition: The round before the semifinals in a knockout competition.
entries.definitionCN: 淘汰赛中半决赛之前的一轮。

entries.definition: A group of four musicians or a piece for four.
entries.definitionCN: 四位乐手组成的团体或为四人写的乐曲。

entries.definition: The ordinal number matching one of four equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 与四等份之一相应的序数词。

entries.definition: An area of a town or country with a clear boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或国家中有明确边界的一片区域。

entries.definition: A fixed period of time in a school or business year.
entries.definitionCN: 学年或商业年度中一段固定的时间。

entries.definition: A length of time with a defined start and end.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确起止的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with the fourth part of a whole and spreads outward to the fourth part of an hour, of a year, of a town and of a game.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从整体的第四份出发，向外扩展到一小时、一年、一座城与一场比赛的第四份。

normal.en: Quarter and quartet both begin from four, one naming a part and the other naming a group of four.
normal.cn: quarter 与 quartet 都从「四」出发，一个指一份，一个指四人的组合。

normal.en: A quarter past the hour is fifteen minutes after it, and a quarter to is fifteen minutes before.
normal.cn: a quarter past 是整点后十五分钟，a quarter to 是整点前十五分钟。

normal.en: Business reports arrive four times a year, so each report covers one quarter.
normal.cn: 商业报表一年来四次，所以每份报表覆盖一个季度。

normal.en: Living quarters keeps the old military sense of lodgings in the plural.
normal.cn: living quarters 以复数保留了旧时军中「营房、住处」的意思。

normal.en: Basketball and American football divide their games into four quarters, each with its own clock.
normal.cn: 篮球和美式橄榄球把比赛分成四节，每一节都有自己的计时。

abstract.en: Dividing a whole into four is the simplest way to make a big thing feel manageable.
abstract.cn: 把一个整体分成四份，是让庞然大物变得可控的最简单办法。

abstract.en: Every quarter of a city has its own memory, which is why the word for a fraction also names a place.
abstract.cn: 城市的每一片街区都有自己的记忆，所以表示分数的词也能指一个地方。

abstract.en: A quarter of an hour is short, yet whole decisions are often made inside it.
abstract.cn: 一刻钟很短，但许多决定往往就在这一刻钟里做成。

examples.en: Only a quarter of the students passed the first test.
examples.cn: 只有四分之一的学生通过了第一次测验。

examples.en: We meet at a quarter to eight every Monday.
examples.cn: 我们每周一七点三刻见面。

examples.en: The company moved its headquarters to the old quarter of the city.
examples.cn: 公司把总部搬到了这座城市的旧城区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阔特」——把一张大饼阔气地切成四块，其中一块就是 quarter，四分之一。

root: 拉丁语 quartus（第四）→ quartarius（第四份）→ 古法语 quartier → 英语 quarter；同族有 quartet、quarterly、quarterfinal。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a fourth part; the senses apply that fourth part to an hour, a year, a town, a game and a set of lodgings.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「第四份」；义项把这份四分之一分别用到一小时、一年、一座城、一场比赛以及一处住处上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round flatbread cut cleanly into four, one piece lifted by a fork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张圆饼被利落地切成四块，其中一块被叉子挑起。

branches.en: a knife crossing a round loaf twice
branches.cn: 一把刀在圆面包上横竖各切一下

branches.en: a clock face split at fifteen-minute marks
branches.cn: 表盘上按十五分钟分出的刻度

branches.en: a report filed four times a year
branches.cn: 一年上交四次的报表

branches.en: a narrow lane behind an old shop
branches.cn: 老店铺后面的一条窄巷

branches.en: a whistle ending a period and a door closing on a barracks
branches.cn: 结束一节的哨声与营房关上的门

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin ordinal for fourth, a noun of portion, the French form and English endings that create time and place words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语序数「第四」、表示份额的名词、法语形式，以及构成时间与地点词的英语词缀搭建起来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quartus is short and regular.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quartus 的拉丁词群短而规整。

definition_zh: 女王；王后；蜂王；纸牌皇后；（棋）后
definition_en: a female ruler of a country; the wife of a king; the single egg-laying female of a bee or ant colony; a playing card with a picture of a queen; the most powerful piece in chess
core_image: 一顶镶着细碎宝石的小冠，放在铺着深色绒布的桌上
scene: 王宫大厅里，侍从为一场加冕礼整理长袍和冠冕，门口的乐师反复校音。The young queen stepped forward to greet her people.
sceneCN: 这里 queen 是「女王」（第 1 个义项：一个国家的女性统治者）；句意为年轻的女王走上前去迎接她的臣民。画面里可留意：长袍、冠冕、门口校音的乐师。

pos.zh: 女王；王后；蜂王；纸牌皇后；（国际象棋）后
使成为女王；（国际象棋）使兵升变为后

derivatives.zh: queen 加 -ly，指有女王气派的、威严而端庄的
queen 加 -ship，指女王的身份或王后之位
queen 与 size 复合，指加大号的床或家具

senses.title: A female ruler
senses.definition: a woman who rules a country in her own right
senses.definitionCN: 凭自身权利统治一个国家的女性
senses.example: The queen opened the new library herself.
senses.exampleCN: 女王亲自为新的图书馆揭幕。
senses.why: Old English cwen first meant woman or wife, and the sense of a ruling woman grew from the wife of a king who could hold power.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cwen 本指女人或妻子，「执政女性」这一义项从可能掌权的国王之妻发展而来。

senses.title: The wife of a king
senses.definition: the wife of a ruling king
senses.definitionCN: 在位国王的妻子
senses.example: The king and queen greeted the guests together.
senses.exampleCN: 国王与王后一起迎接客人。
senses.why: The oldest use of the word for a royal woman was as the partner of a king, and that sense remains in titles.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指王室女性最古老的用法是作为国王的配偶，这层意思仍留在正式称谓里。

senses.title: The egg-laying female of a colony
senses.definition: the single female in a colony of bees or ants that lays all the eggs
senses.definitionCN: 蜂群或蚁群中唯一产卵的雌性个体
senses.example: The workers feed the queen and keep her in the warmest part of the nest.
senses.exampleCN: 工蜂喂养蜂王，并把她安置在巢中最暖和的地方。
senses.why: The one reproductive female of a colony holds a position like a ruler, so keepers gave her the royal name.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体中唯一负责繁殖的雌性地位如同统治者，养蜂人便给了她这个王室称呼。

senses.title: A playing card
senses.definition: the card in a set of playing cards that carries a picture of a queen
senses.definitionCN: 一副纸牌上印有王后画像的那张牌
senses.example: She won the trick with the queen of hearts.
senses.exampleCN: 她用红桃皇后赢下了这一墩。
senses.why: Card makers ranked the court cards, and the female figure beside the king took the word queen.
senses.whyCN: 纸牌制作者给宫廷牌排了等级，国王身旁的女性形象就用了 queen 这个词。

senses.title: The strongest chess piece
senses.definition: the chess piece that can move any number of squares in any straight line
senses.definitionCN: 能在任意直线上走任意格数的国际象棋棋子
senses.example: A pawn that reaches the far rank may become a queen.
senses.exampleCN: 走到对方底线的兵可以升变为后。
senses.why: The piece was once called the queen because it stood beside the king and moved with great freedom, and the name outlived its origin.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子当初因侍立在国王身旁、行走极为自由而被称为后，名字比它的由来活得更久。

intro.en: Queen is a native English word from Old English cwen, originally meaning woman or wife and related to words for woman in other old European languages.
intro.cn: queen 是英语本族词，来自古英语 cwen，本指女人或妻子，与欧洲其他古老语言中表示女人的词同源。

items.en: Cwen meant woman or wife, a neutral word for a female person.
items.cn: cwen 意为女人或妻子，是对女性中性的称呼。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic as a term for woman, with relatives in other northern languages.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为表示女人的词，在其他北方语言中有亲属词。

items.en: Middle English quen narrowed to the wife of a king and to a woman of royal rank.
items.cn: 中古英语 quen 收窄为国王之妻以及有王室身份的女性。

items.en: The spelling settled as queen, and the word spread to the female head of a colony and to cards and chess.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 queen，词义扩展到群体的雌性首领以及纸牌与国际象棋。

items.en: Modern English keeps the royal senses and the figurative senses of a leading woman or a dominant female animal.
items.cn: 现代英语保留王室义，也保留「杰出女性」与「群体中占主导的雌性动物」这类引申义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms that grew from the same word; the near-meaning group collects titles and words for female rulers.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个词生长出来的形式；近义组收表示女性统治者与称号的词。

entries.definition: Having the dignity of a queen.
entries.definitionCN: 具有女王般威严的。

entries.definition: The position or rank of a queen.
entries.definitionCN: 女王的地位或身份。

entries.definition: Larger than standard, used of beds.
entries.definitionCN: 大于标准尺寸的，用于床。

entries.definition: An archaic word for a bold or disreputable woman.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指大胆或名声不好的女人。

entries.definition: A king, queen or emperor who rules a state.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个国家的国王、女王或皇帝。

entries.definition: A woman who rules an empire.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个帝国的女性。

entries.definition: The spouse of a reigning king or queen.
entries.definitionCN: 在位国王或女王的配偶。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country.
entries.definitionCN: 治理国家的人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a plain term for a woman and rose to the throne; from the throne it spread to bees, cards and chess.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从对女人的平常称呼升上王座；又从王座扩散到蜜蜂、纸牌与国际象棋。

normal.en: Queen and quean look almost the same, but quean is an old insult while queen is a title.
normal.cn: queen 与 quean 拼写几乎一样，但 quean 是旧时的贬称，queen 是尊号。

normal.en: Queenly describes the manner of a queen, while queenship names her rank.
normal.cn: queenly 描述女王的气度，queenship 指她的身份。

normal.en: A queen bee is the only female in the hive that lays eggs, so the hive depends on her alone.
normal.cn: 蜂王是蜂巢中唯一产卵的雌蜂，整个蜂巢都靠她一个。

normal.en: The queen of hearts is a card, but the phrase also names a woman who wins hearts.
normal.cn: the queen of hearts 既是纸牌，也用来指赢得人心的女子。

normal.en: In chess the queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined, which makes her the strongest piece.
normal.cn: 国际象棋的皇后走法相当于车与象的合体，因此是最强的棋子。

abstract.en: A word for woman became a word for power, and the old plain meaning disappeared from ordinary speech.
abstract.cn: 一个指女人的词变成了指权力的词，而原先那个朴素含义从日常口语里消失了。

abstract.en: The queen in a hive rules by being the only source of the next generation, not by giving orders.
abstract.cn: 蜂巢里的蜂王靠成为下一代的唯一来源而「统治」，并不发号施令。

abstract.en: In chess the strongest piece is guarded most carefully, which says something about how power is kept.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上最强的棋子被保护得最小心，这本身就说明了权力是如何被守住的。

examples.en: The queen waved from the balcony as the crowd cheered.
examples.cn: 女王在阳台上挥手，人群欢呼。

examples.en: Only the queen of a hive lays eggs.
examples.cn: 蜂巢里只有蜂王产卵。

examples.en: He promoted the pawn to a queen and won the endgame.
examples.cn: 他把兵升变为后，赢下了残局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「葵恩」——像向日葵一样被众人仰望的那位女性，就是 queen，女王。

root: 古英语 cwen（女人、妻子）→ 中古英语 quen（王后）→ 现代英语 queen；同族有 queenly、queenship、quean。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woman of highest rank; the senses divide into a ruler, a royal wife, the female head of a colony, a card and a chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是地位最高的女性；义项分为统治者、王室配偶、群体雌性首领、纸牌与棋子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small jewelled crown resting on dark velvet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶镶着细碎宝石的小冠，放在深色绒布上。

branches.en: a hand raised to quiet a hall
branches.cn: 一只举起让大厅安静的手

branches.en: two thrones set side by side
branches.cn: 并排放着的两把王座

branches.en: a single bee at the centre of a comb
branches.cn: 蜂巢中央唯一的那只蜂

branches.en: a card turned face up on a table
branches.cn: 桌上翻开的一张牌

branches.en: a piece sweeping the whole board
branches.cn: 一枚横扫整个棋盘的棋子

intro.en: The word is native English, so its structure is mostly the old root plus English endings that name manner, rank and size.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，结构主要是古老词根加上表示气度、身份与尺寸的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 问题；提问；试题；议题；疑问；质疑
definition_en: a sentence that asks for information; a problem set in a test; a matter that needs discussion; doubt about something; to ask someone about something, often with doubt
core_image: 一张被反复折叠的纸，边上写着一个大大的问号
scene: 律师把文件推到桌子中间，指着其中一行，向证人提出一个必须当场回答的问题。The lawyer asked a question that made the whole room go silent.
sceneCN: 这里 question 是「提问、问题」（第 1 个义项：向别人索取信息的问句）；句意为律师提出的那个问题让整个房间安静下来。画面里可留意：文件、指着一行字的手指、沉默的旁听者。

pos.zh: 问题；提问；试题；议题；疑问

derivatives.zh: question 加 -able，指可疑的、未必可靠的
question 加 -ing，指带着疑问的、追问的
与 question 同族，指一份列出问题供人填写的调查表
un- 加 questionable，指无可质疑的

senses.title: A sentence that asks for information
senses.definition: a sentence or phrase used to ask for information or an answer
senses.definitionCN: 用来索取信息或要求回答的句子或短语
senses.example: She asked a question about the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她就日程安排提了一个问题。
senses.why: Latin quaestio named the act of seeking, and the English word first names the words used when someone seeks an answer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 quaestio 指「寻求」这一行为，英语这个词首先指人们寻求答案时说出的那些话。

senses.title: A problem in a test
senses.definition: a problem or task set in an examination to be answered
senses.definitionCN: 考试中设置出来、需要作答的题目
senses.example: The last question was harder than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一道题比其余的更难。
senses.why: An examination asks many things of the student, so each item on the paper is also one of those asks.
senses.whyCN: 考试向学生提出许多「问」，于是试卷上的每一道题也是一次这样的「问」。

senses.title: A matter that needs settling
senses.definition: a subject or matter that people must discuss and decide
senses.definitionCN: 人们必须讨论并作出决定的事项
senses.example: The question of funding is still open.
senses.exampleCN: 经费问题仍然悬而未决。
senses.why: A matter under discussion is treated as a thing put before the group to be answered, so it too is called a question.
senses.whyCN: 被讨论的事项被当作摆在众人面前、等待回答的东西，所以它也被称作 question。

senses.title: Doubt about something
senses.definition: a feeling of uncertainty about whether something is true or right
senses.definitionCN: 对某事是否真实或正确感到不确定
senses.example: There is no question about her honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诚实是毫无疑问的。
senses.why: If a matter is still open to being asked about, then certainty is missing, and the word comes to name that missing certainty.
senses.whyCN: 一件事如果仍可被追问，就说明确定感缺席，于是这个词转而指这种缺席的确定感。

senses.title: To ask someone about something
senses.definition: to ask a person about something, especially when you doubt the answer
senses.definitionCN: 向某人询问某事，尤其在怀疑其说法时
senses.example: The police questioned him for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 警察盘问了他一个小时。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into action: putting questions to a person, often to test whether their account holds.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词化为动作：向某人连续发问，常常是为了检验其说法是否站得住。

intro.en: Question comes from the Latin noun for a seeking or inquiry, built on the verb to seek, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: question 源自拉丁语表示「寻求、探究」的名词，由动词「寻求」构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, to search for, and it stands behind a large family of words about asking and investigating.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、寻找，它支撑着一大批关于询问与调查的词。

items.en: Quaestio named the act of seeking and, in law and debate, the matter put forward for an answer.
items.cn: quaestio 指寻求的行为，在法律与辩论中指提出来等待回答的事项。

items.en: Old French question kept both the act of asking and the subject under dispute.
items.cn: 古法语 question 同时保留了「发问」这一行为与「争议中的事项」这两层意思。

items.en: Middle English used the word for an utterance that asks, for a test item and for a doubtful matter.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指发问的话语、试题以及可疑的事项。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb to question, meaning to interrogate or to cast doubt on a claim.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词用法，意为审问或对某项主张表示怀疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin stem of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers words for inquiries, doubts and disputed matters.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「寻求」词干上的词；近义组收表示询问、怀疑与争议事项的词。

entries.definition: Open to doubt or suspicion.
entries.definitionCN: 可怀疑的；有问题的。

entries.definition: A written set of questions used to collect information.
entries.definitionCN: 用于收集信息的一套书面问题。

entries.definition: A long search for something important.
entries.definitionCN: 为重要目标进行的长期寻找。

entries.definition: A question, especially one raising a doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 问题，尤指提出疑问的问题。

entries.definition: The act of asking for information.
entries.definitionCN: 询问、打听信息的行为。

entries.definition: A subject that people are discussing or arguing about.
entries.definitionCN: 人们正在讨论或争论的话题。

entries.definition: A feeling that something may not be true.
entries.definitionCN: 觉得某事可能不真实的感觉。

entries.definition: A difficulty that needs to be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 需要解决的困难。

normalIntro.en: The word started as the act of seeking an answer and grew into the sentence, the test item, the disputed matter and the doubt itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「寻求答案」这一行为出发，长成问句、试题、争议事项，最后连怀疑本身也叫这个名字。

normal.en: Question and quest share the Latin verb to seek: a question is a small search for an answer.
normal.cn: question 与 quest 共用拉丁语动词「寻求」：一个问题就是一次寻找答案的小旅程。

normal.en: A question mark is literally the written sign of a question, and it turns a statement into an ask.
normal.cn: 问号字面上就是问题的书写符号，它把陈述变成发问。

normal.en: Out of the question means not even worth discussing, as if the matter has been closed before any answer.
normal.cn: out of the question 意为连讨论都不必，好像在得到回答之前事情已经关闭。

normal.en: Questionable means able to be questioned, so a questionable claim is one that invites doubt.
normal.cn: questionable 意为「可被追问的」，所以可疑的说法就是招来怀疑的说法。

normal.en: To question a person is to put a series of questions to them, often to test their story.
normal.cn: to question 一个人就是向他连续发问，常常是为了检验他的说法。

abstract.en: A good question does not merely ask for an answer; it redraws the space in which an answer can be found.
abstract.cn: 好问题不只索取答案，它还重新划出答案可以被找到的那片空间。

abstract.en: Every test item assumes there is one right answer, while a real question often has several.
abstract.cn: 每道试题都假定只有一个正确答案，而真正的问题常常有好几个。

abstract.en: Doubt and inquiry share one word because asking and not knowing are two sides of the same act.
abstract.cn: 怀疑与询问共用一个词，因为发问与不知道本就是同一动作的两面。

examples.en: May I ask a question before we begin?
examples.cn: 开始之前我可以问一个问题吗？

examples.en: Question three on the paper asked for a short explanation.
examples.cn: 试卷第三题要求作简要说明。

examples.en: Nobody questioned the figures, though several people looked uneasy.
examples.cn: 没有人质疑那些数字，尽管有几个人显得不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快试称」——遇到问题先快试着称一称分量，再回答，记住 question 是问题、提问。

root: 拉丁语 quaerere（寻求）→ quaestio（探究、问题）→ 古法语 question → 英语 question；同族有 quest、query、questionnaire。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a search for an answer; the senses split into the spoken ask, the test item, the matter to be settled, the doubt and the act of interrogating.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「寻求答案」；义项分为口头发问、试题、待解决的事项、怀疑，以及审问这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a much-folded sheet of paper with a large question mark in the margin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被反复折叠的纸，页边画着一个大大的问号。

branches.en: a hand raised in a classroom
branches.cn: 教室里举起的一只手

branches.en: a numbered line on an exam paper
branches.cn: 试卷上一道编号的题目

branches.en: a folder marked pending on a desk
branches.cn: 桌上标着「待定」的文件夹

branches.en: a pause before an answer
branches.cn: 回答之前的那一顿

branches.en: a lamp left on in an interview room
branches.cn: 审讯室里亮着的一盏灯

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin verb to seek, its noun of action, the French form and English endings that name doubt and repetition.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语动词「寻求」、由它构成的动作名词、法语形式，以及表示怀疑与反复的英语词尾支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around quaerere is wide, and a few of its members are still in English.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 quaerere 的拉丁词群很宽，其中几个成员仍留在英语里。

items.meaning: a doubt put as a question

definition_zh: 队伍；排队；队列；（旧）辫子
definition_en: a line of people waiting for something; to wait in such a line; a list of items handled in the order they arrive, especially in computing; a long plait of hair
core_image: 雨里一条沿着墙根排开的长队，伞尖连成一线
scene: 剧院门外，雨点打在伞面上，人们把伞收低，一个接一个站在售票窗口前的长队里。A long queue stretched along the wet pavement outside the theatre.
sceneCN: 这里 queue 是「排队等候的队伍」（第 1 个义项：一列等待的人）；句意为一条长队沿着剧院外湿漉漉的路面延伸开去。画面里可留意：伞面、湿路面、连成一线的人。

derivatives.zh: queue 加 -ing，指排队等候这件事或排队系统
queue 加 -er，指排队的人
queue 与 jumper 复合，指插队的人

senses.title: A line of people waiting
senses.definition: a line of people standing one behind another while waiting for something
senses.definitionCN: 人们一个接一个站着等待某物的行列
senses.example: A long queue formed outside the ticket office.
senses.exampleCN: 售票处外排起了长队。
senses.why: Old French cue meant a tail, and a line of waiting people was seen as a tail trailing from a counter.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 cue 意为尾巴，一列等待的人被看作从柜台后拖出来的一条尾巴。

senses.title: To wait in a line
senses.definition: to stand in a line and wait for your turn
senses.definitionCN: 站在队伍里等候轮到自己
senses.example: We queued for two hours in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们冒雨排了两个小时的队。
senses.why: Once the noun named the line, the verb naturally named the act of standing in it.
senses.whyCN: 名词既然指这条队伍，动词自然就指站在队伍里等候这一动作。

senses.title: A list handled in arrival order
senses.definition: a store of items in which the first one to arrive is the first one to be handled
senses.definitionCN: 一种存储结构，先到达的项先被处理
senses.example: The printer keeps every job in a queue until the paper is loaded.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机把每个任务都放进队列，直到装好纸才处理。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the image of people waiting in a line, because a queue serves first come, first served.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了人们排队等候的形象，因为队列正是先到先服务。

senses.title: A long plait of hair
senses.definition: a long braid of hair worn hanging down the back, as in older portraits
senses.definitionCN: 垂在背后的长发辫，见于旧时画像
senses.example: In the old portrait her hair hangs in a long queue.
senses.exampleCN: 在那幅旧画像里，她的头发梳成一条长辫垂在背后。
senses.why: The tail sense of the French word survived in English for a plait of hair, which really does hang like a tail.
senses.whyCN: 法语词中「尾巴」这层意思在英语里保留下来，用来指辫子，而辫子确实像尾巴一样垂着。

intro.en: Queue is a French word built on the Latin word for tail, and its journey from tail to waiting line explains most of its senses.
intro.cn: queue 是法语词，建立在拉丁语表示「尾巴」的词上；从尾巴到队伍这段路程解释了它的大部分义项。

items.en: Cauda meant the tail of an animal, and it stands behind several words about things that trail behind.
items.cn: cauda 指动物的尾巴，它支撑着好几个表示「拖在后面之物」的词。

items.en: Old French cue meant a tail and also a line of people or vehicles waiting one behind another.
items.cn: 古法语 cue 既指尾巴，也指人或车辆一辆接一辆等候的行列。

items.en: The later French spelling queue carried both the tail and the waiting-line senses across the Channel.
items.cn: 较晚的法语拼写 queue 把「尾巴」与「等候行列」两层意思一起带过了海峡。

items.en: English took the word for the waiting line, kept the old tail sense for a plait of hair, and later applied it to computer lists.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个词的「等候行列」义，保留「尾巴」义来指发辫，后来又把它用到计算机列表上。

items.en: Modern British English uses queue for almost any orderly line, while American English usually prefers line.
items.cn: 现代英式英语几乎用 queue 指任何有秩序的队伍，而美式英语通常更爱用 line。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same word and its close homophone; the near-meaning group gathers words for lines and waiting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的各种形式以及它的近音词；近义组收表示队伍与等待的词。

entries.definition: A signal that tells someone when to act or speak.
entries.definitionCN: 提示某人何时行动或说话的信号。

entries.definition: The act of standing in a queue.
entries.definitionCN: 排队等候的行为。

entries.definition: A person who is waiting in a queue.
entries.definitionCN: 在队伍里等候的人。

entries.definition: Someone who takes a place ahead of those already waiting.
entries.definitionCN: 越过已等候者抢先占位的人。

entries.definition: A row of people or things one behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 一个接一个排成行的人或物。

entries.definition: A number of things arranged side by side.
entries.definitionCN: 并排排列的一串事物。

entries.definition: A line of people moving one behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 一人接一人前进的行列。

entries.definition: To stay in place until something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 留在原地直到某事发生。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a tail and became a line of people, which is why a queue and an animal's tail share a picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从尾巴开始，变成了人群的行列，所以队列与动物尾巴共享同一幅画面。

normal.en: Queue and cue sound the same, but a cue tells you when to act while a queue is where you wait to act.
normal.cn: queue 与 cue 同音，但 cue 告诉你何时行动，queue 是你等待行动的地方。

normal.en: The silent letters after q are a reminder that the word came from French, where the tail still shows in the spelling.
normal.cn: q 后面那些不发音的字母提醒你这个词来自法语，尾巴的痕迹还留在拼写里。

normal.en: Queue up and join the queue describe the same act, one as a verb and one as a noun.
normal.cn: queue up 与 join the queue 描述同一个动作，一个用动词，一个用名词。

normal.en: A printer queue works first come, first served, exactly like a line of people at a window.
normal.cn: 打印机队列先到先处理，和窗口前排队的人一模一样。

normal.en: British speakers queue; American speakers usually stand in line.
normal.cn: 英国人用 queue，美国人通常说 stand in line。

abstract.en: A queue is a promise that order will be respected, and the promise is what makes waiting bearable.
abstract.cn: 队伍是一种「秩序会被尊重」的承诺，正是这个承诺让等待变得可以忍受。

abstract.en: Jumping the queue is a small act that reveals how much of society rests on strangers trusting a line.
abstract.cn: 插队这个小小的举动，暴露出社会有多少部分建立在对陌生人所排队伍的信任上。

abstract.en: To queue is to give up time now in exchange for a turn later, the plainest trade there is.
abstract.cn: 排队就是用现在的时间换将来的轮次，这是最朴素的一种交换。

examples.en: The queue for the concert stretched around the corner.
examples.cn: 音乐会的队伍拐过街角。

examples.en: We had to queue for nearly an hour.
examples.cn: 我们不得不排了将近一个小时的队。

examples.en: The print queue is empty, so the document should come out at once.
examples.cn: 打印队列是空的，所以文件应该会立刻打出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「Q」——队伍排得像一个大写的 Q，尾巴拖得长长的，记住 queue 是队伍、排队。

root: 拉丁语 cauda（尾巴）→ 古法语 cue（尾巴、行列）→ 法语 queue → 英语 queue；同族有 cue 的近音形式与 queueing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a tail-like line; the senses divide into the waiting line, the act of waiting, a computing list and an old plait of hair.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是像尾巴一样拖着的行列；义项分为等候的队伍、排队这一动作、计算机队列，以及旧时的长辫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line along a wall in the rain, umbrella tips touching.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中沿墙排开的长队，伞尖彼此相触。

branches.en: a rope of people down a wet street
branches.cn: 湿街上一条由人组成的绳索

branches.en: feet shifting slowly forward
branches.cn: 慢慢向前挪动的脚步

branches.en: a list fed in at one end
branches.cn: 从一端送入的清单

branches.en: a tail hanging down a back
branches.cn: 垂在背后的一条尾巴

branches.en: the same word for an animal's tail and a printer's list
branches.cn: 同一个词既指动物尾巴，也指打印机清单

intro.en: The word is a French borrowing whose Latin base means tail, with English endings that name the activity and the people involved.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语借词，其拉丁词基意为尾巴，再加上表示活动与参与者的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base cauda gave the French word its tail sense, and that single image holds the whole family together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 cauda 给法语词带来了尾巴义，就是这一个意象把整族词连在一起。

definition_en: moving or happening at great speed; able to think or notice fast; lasting only a short time; easily made angry; alive, in an old use
core_image: 一只掠过水面的蜻蜓，翅膀几乎看不清
scene: 清晨的厨房里，水壶刚响，她一边系围裙一边把面包推进烤槽。A quick breakfast was all she had time for before the bus came.
sceneCN: 这里 quick 是「短暂的、匆匆的」（第 3 个义项：只持续很短时间）；句意为在公交车来之前，她只来得及吃一顿匆匆的早餐。画面里可留意：响了的水壶、半系的围裙、烤槽里的面包。

pos.zh: 快的；迅速的；敏捷的；短暂的；急躁的

quick 加 -en，指加快、使活跃
quick 加 -ness，指迅速、敏捷

senses.title: Moving or happening fast
senses.definition: moving, acting or happening with high speed
senses.definitionCN: 以很高的速度移动、行动或发生
senses.example: She gave a quick reply and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她迅速回答了一句就离开了房间。
senses.why: Old English cwic meant alive, and lively movement is the first thing the word came to describe.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 cwic 意为「活着的」，而活物最显眼的表现就是动作迅速，这是这个词最先用来描述的东西。

senses.title: Able to think or notice fast
senses.definition: able to understand or notice something in a very short time
senses.definitionCN: 能在极短时间内理解或察觉
senses.example: He has a quick mind for figures.
senses.exampleCN: 他对数字反应很快。
senses.why: A lively body and a lively mind were both described with the word for alive, so mental speed joined physical speed.
senses.whyCN: 活的身体与活的头脑都用「活着」这个词来描述，于是心智的敏捷也加入了身体的速度义。

senses.title: Lasting only a short time
senses.definition: taking or lasting only a little time
senses.definitionCN: 只花或只持续很少的时间
senses.example: We took a quick look at the map before we left.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前我们匆匆看了一眼地图。
senses.why: If an action is fast, it also ends soon, so the word came to describe anything brief rather than merely fast.
senses.whyCN: 一个动作既然快，也就会很快结束，于是这个词转而形容任何短暂之物，而不只是形容速度快。

senses.title: Easily made angry
senses.definition: tending to become angry very suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 很容易突然发怒的
senses.example: He has a quick temper and regrets it at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他脾气急躁，发完火马上就后悔。
senses.why: A quick temper ignites fast, and the same adjective for speed was applied to the speed of anger rather than of motion.
senses.whyCN: 急性子发火快，于是这个表示速度的形容词被用到愤怒的速度上，而不是移动的速度上。

senses.title: Alive, in old use
senses.definition: living, in language that survives mainly in old texts and set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 活着的，主要保留在旧文本与固定说法中
senses.example: The old sermon spoke of the quick and the dead.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的布道讲到了生者与死者。
senses.why: Cwic meant alive in Old English, and this oldest sense now survives only in fixed phrases and in the saying the quick and the dead.
senses.whyCN: cwic 在古英语中就是「活着的」，这一最古老的意思如今只留在固定说法与 the quick and the dead 这句里。

intro.en: Quick is a native English word whose oldest meaning was alive; the sense of speed grew from the liveliness of living things.
intro.cn: quick 是英语本族词，最古老的意思是「活着的」；速度义是从活物的活跃状态生长出来的。

items.en: Cwic meant alive or living, and it described people, animals and even running water.
items.cn: cwic 意为活着的、有生命的，可形容人、动物，甚至流动的水。

items.en: The word is reconstructed in older Germanic with the same sense of alive, and related forms appear in other northern languages.
items.cn: 这个词在更早的日耳曼语中被重构为同样的「活着」义，其他北方语言中也有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English quick widened from alive to lively, and from lively to fast.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quick 从「活着」扩展到「活跃」，又从「活跃」扩展到「快」。

items.en: The speed sense became dominant, while the sense of alive retreated into set phrases such as the quick and the dead.
items.cn: 速度义成为主导，而「活着」义退入 the quick and the dead 这类固定说法。

items.en: Modern English adds the senses of a short duration, of a sharp mind and of a short temper.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了持续时间短、脑筋快、脾气急这几层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same old root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of speed and alertness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古老词根上的形式；近义组收表示速度与机敏的形容词。

entries.definition: At high speed.
entries.definitionCN: 以很快的速度。

entries.definition: To make or become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 使变快或变快。

entries.definition: The quality of being fast.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速、敏捷的性质。

entries.definition: Loose sand that swallows what stands on it.
entries.definitionCN: 会吞没立足之物的流沙，其中 quick 仍是「活的」旧义。

entries.definition: Moving or done at high speed.
entries.definitionCN: 高速移动或完成的。

entries.definition: Happening in a very short time.
entries.definitionCN: 在极短时间内发生的。

entries.definition: Moving smoothly and quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 平稳而迅速地移动的。

entries.definition: Done without delay.
entries.definitionCN: 毫不拖延地完成的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as alive, moved to lively, then to fast, and finally to brief; each step is shorter than the one before.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「活着」开始，走到「活跃」，再到「快」，最后到「短暂」；每一步都比上一步更短。

normal.en: Quick and quicksand share the old sense of alive: quicksand behaves like something living because it shifts and swallows.
normal.cn: quick 与 quicksand 共用旧义「活的」：流沙会移动、会吞没，行为像活物。

normal.en: Quickly is the adverb, quicken the verb, quickness the noun: three endings from one short root.
normal.cn: quickly 是副词，quicken 是动词，quickness 是名词：一个短词根带出三个词尾。

normal.en: A quick temper is a temper that ignites fast, not a temper that lasts long.
normal.cn: a quick temper 指点火快的脾气，不是持续久的脾气。

normal.en: The quick and the dead is the one common phrase where quick still means alive.
normal.cn: the quick and the dead 是 quick 仍然表示「活着的」的唯一常见说法。

normal.en: Quick to learn describes the speed of learning, while a quick study describes the person who learns fast.
normal.cn: quick to learn 描述学习的速度，而 a quick study 指学得快的人。

abstract.en: Speed began as a sign of life, and the modern word keeps that trace in phrases about the living.
abstract.cn: 速度最初是生命的标志，现代这个词仍在关于生者的说法里留着那道痕迹。

abstract.en: A quick answer can be a sign of a sharp mind or of a careless one, and the word alone cannot tell which.
abstract.cn: 迅速的回答既可能是脑筋敏锐，也可能是草率，光凭这个词分辨不出来。

abstract.en: To call someone quick is to praise a body and a mind at once, as if they moved on the same clock.
abstract.cn: 说一个人 quick，是同时称赞身体与头脑，仿佛它们走在同一只钟上。

examples.en: He took a quick shower and ran for the train.
examples.cn: 他匆匆冲了个澡就去赶火车。

examples.en: She is quick at catching small mistakes in a text.
examples.cn: 她很善于抓住文章里的小错误。

examples.en: Be careful with him; he has a quick temper.
examples.cn: 和他打交道要小心，他脾气很急。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快克」——快客一到，事情立刻办完，记住 quick 是快的、迅速的。

root: 古英语 cwic（活着的）→ 中古英语 quick（活跃的）→ 现代英语 quick（快的、短暂的）；同族有 quickly、quicken、quicksand。

sensesIntro.en: The core is liveliness; the senses move from being alive to moving fast, to thinking fast, to lasting briefly, to a fast temper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「活跃」；义项从活着走向动作快，再到思维快、持续时间短，最后到脾气急。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dragonfly skimming the water, its wings almost too fast to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只掠过水面的蜻蜓，翅膀快得几乎看不清。

branches.en: a foot landing before the eye follows
branches.cn: 眼睛还没跟上，脚已经落地

branches.en: an answer given before the question ends
branches.cn: 问题还没问完就给出的回答

branches.en: a glance at a map at a bus stop
branches.cn: 在公交站匆匆看一眼地图

branches.en: a match struck and already burning
branches.cn: 火柴一划就已燃起

branches.en: the same speed, once admired and once feared
branches.cn: 同一种速度，一次被赞赏，一次被畏惧

intro.en: The word is native English and carries its meaning through a short root plus endings for adverbs, verbs and nouns.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，靠一个短词根加上副词、动词与名词词尾来承载词义。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 迅速地；立刻；敏捷地
definition_en: at high speed; after only a short time; with a fast mind or fast reaction
core_image: 秒针扫过表盘，几乎来不及看清刻度
scene: 厨房里水开了，她一手关火，一手把面条下进锅里，动作没有半点停顿。She quickly moved the pot off the burner before the water boiled over.
sceneCN: 这里 quickly 是「迅速地、动作很快地」（第 1 个义项：以很高的速度做某事）；句意为她迅速把锅从炉子上移开，免得水溢出来。画面里可留意：关火的手、下锅的面条、腾起的白汽。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，指快的、敏捷的
quick 加 -en，指加快、使活跃
quick 加 -ness，指迅速、敏捷的性质

senses.title: At high speed
senses.definition: at a high speed, so that little time is taken
senses.definitionCN: 以很高的速度，因此只花很少时间
senses.example: She finished the test quickly and checked her answers.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快做完试卷，又检查了一遍答案。
senses.why: The adverb simply adds the manner ending to the adjective of speed, so it describes how an action is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是在表示速度的形容词后加了方式词尾，因此描述动作是以什么方式进行的。

senses.title: After only a short time
senses.definition: within a short time after something else happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生后很短的时间内
senses.example: The sky darkened quickly before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，天色很快就暗了下来。
senses.why: Speed in time is also speed of change, so quickly can mark how soon a new state appears.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的快也是变化上的快，所以 quickly 可以标记一种新状态出现得有多早。

senses.title: With a fast mind
senses.definition: in a way that shows fast thinking or fast noticing
senses.definitionCN: 以显出思维或察觉很快的方式
senses.example: She quickly saw what the problem was.
senses.exampleCN: 她很快就看出问题出在哪里。
senses.why: The adjective also described a lively mind, and the adverb carries that mental sense alongside physical speed.
senses.whyCN: 形容词也形容头脑灵活，副词就把这层心智义与身体的速度义一起带上。

intro.en: Quickly is the adjective quick with the English manner suffix -ly; its history is the history of quick itself.
intro.cn: quickly 是形容词 quick 加上英语方式词尾 -ly；它的历史就是 quick 本身的历史。

items.en: The root cwic meant alive, and it is the source of the whole family.
items.cn: 词根 cwic 意为活着的，是整族词的源头。

items.en: Quick moved from alive to lively and then to fast, and adverbs of manner were formed from it.
items.cn: quick 从「活着」走到「活跃」，再到「快」，方式副词也就由它构成。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, naming the manner in which something is done.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变成副词，指出做某事的方式。

items.en: Quickly settled as the standard adverb of speed, beside the older phrase in quick time.
items.cn: quickly 固定为表示速度的标准副词，与较早的说法 in quick time 并存。

items.en: Modern English uses quickly for physical speed, for short delay and for mental alertness.
items.cn: 现代英语用 quickly 指身体速度、短暂延迟与心智的机敏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of speed and promptness.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词及其亲属形式；近义组收表示速度与及时性的副词。

entries.definition: Fast, brief or easily angered.
entries.definitionCN: 快的、短暂的或易怒的。

entries.definition: To make or become faster.
entries.definitionCN: 使变快或变快。

entries.definition: The quality of being fast.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速、敏捷的性质。

entries.definition: Loose sand that swallows what stands on it.
entries.definitionCN: 会吞没立足之物的流沙。

entries.definition: At a very fast rate.
entries.definitionCN: 以极快的速率。

entries.definition: Smoothly and at speed.
entries.definitionCN: 平稳而迅速地。

entries.definition: Without any delay.
entries.definitionCN: 毫不拖延地。

entries.definition: At high speed, often of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 高速地，常指移动。

normalIntro.en: The word is the plain adverb of quick; every sense follows from the idea of little time being used.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 quick 的普通副词；每一层意思都从「只用了很少时间」这一想法引出。

normal.en: Quickly is quick plus -ly, and the suffix simply tells you that the word now describes how something is done.
normal.cn: quickly 就是 quick 加 -ly，这个后缀只是告诉你，这个词现在描述事情是怎样做的。

normal.en: More quickly and most quickly are the comparatives, because a two-syllable adverb prefers more over -er.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more quickly 与 most quickly，因为双音节副词更倾向用 more 而不用 -er。

normal.en: As quickly as possible is the standard phrase for doing something at the greatest safe speed.
normal.cn: as quickly as possible 是做某事时「在安全前提下尽快」的标准说法。

normal.en: Quickly can describe a mind as well as a body, as in she quickly saw the point.
normal.cn: quickly 既能描述身体也能描述头脑，如她很快抓住了要点。

normal.en: Placed at the start of a sentence, quickly often signals that the next event followed at once.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，quickly 常常表示紧接着就发生了下一件事。

abstract.en: An adverb of speed quietly tells us what the speaker values: some things should be done quickly, others never.
abstract.cn: 一个表示速度的副词悄悄透露了说话者的价值判断：有些事应当尽快做，有些则永远不该。

abstract.en: Quickly and well are often set against each other, though the best work sometimes manages both.
abstract.cn: 快与好常被摆在对立面，尽管最好的工作有时两者兼得。

abstract.en: To say that something happened quickly is also to say that there was little time to notice it happening.
abstract.cn: 说某事发生得快，也等于说几乎没留下让人察觉它的时间。

examples.en: He quickly shut the window when the rain started.
examples.cn: 雨一开始下，他就迅速关上了窗。

examples.en: The rumour spread quickly through the small town.
examples.cn: 谣言很快传遍了这座小镇。

examples.en: She quickly realized that the address was wrong.
examples.cn: 她很快意识到地址写错了。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「用的时间少」；义项分为身体的速度、短暂的延迟与快速的思维。

core.cn: 核心意象：秒针扫过刻度，快得几乎读不出来。

branches.cn: 在水溢出前把锅端起

branches.cn: 几分钟内转灰的天空

branches.en: a problem understood at a glance
branches.cn: 一眼就看懂的问题

branches.en: the same short span of time seen from outside and from inside
branches.cn: 同一段短促时间，从外面看与从里面看

branches.en: a fast hand guided by a fast eye
branches.cn: 被快眼引导的快手
